title: Cascade Deep Learning (nnU-Net + ResNet-18) for Meniscus Segmentation and Three-Grade Injury Classification on Knee MRI: A Single-Centre Study with Reader Assistance Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate detection and grading of meniscal injury guide treatment, but MRI interpretation is time-consuming and subject to interobserver variability. We developed and evaluated a cascade deep-learning framework that segments the menisci and grades their status (healthy, degenerative, grade-III tear) on knee MRI, and assessed its value as a reader-assistance tool. Methods In this single-centre retrospective study, 562 patients (608 knees; 1,216 coronal and sagittal sequences) scanned on a 1.5-T system between 2018 and 2022 were included. A 3D nnU-Net segmented the medial and lateral menisci. Subsequently, the segmented regions of interest were classified by a 2D ResNet-18 into three grades, and coronal and sagittal predictions were fused by a most-severe-class rule.The dataset was partitioned at the patient level into an 80% training set and a 20% held-out test set. Model performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), accuracy, F1 score, and the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In a multi-reader study, two junior readers diagnosed 100 cases, first unaided and subsequently, following a two-week washout period, with AI assistance (probabilities and Grad-CAM maps). Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity for grade-III tears, reading time, and inter-reader agreement were compared using the McNemar test and Cohen’s κ. Results The nnU-Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.84 for intact menisci, but only 0.32–0.40 for injured menisci. For binary detection (torn vs. non-torn), the fusion model reached an accuracy of 73.77% (F1-score: 72.88%), with the coronal plane outperforming the sagittal plane (F1-score: 76.29% vs. 68.83%; AUC: 0.79 vs. 0.71); the three-grade accuracy was 68.01%. With AI assistance, the accuracy of junior readers increased from 64.0% to 78.0% (McNemar χ² = 7.68, P < 0.01), sensitivity for grade-III tears improved from 60.0% to 80.0%, reading time decreased by 38% (from 44.7 ± 11.2 to 27.9 ± 7.4 s/case), and interobserver agreement improved from κ = 0.52 to 0.68. Conclusion The cascade nnU-Net + ResNet-18 framework performed meniscus segmentation and injury grading with moderate standalone accuracy but demonstrated a clear assistive benefit, improving the sensitivity and efficiency of junior readers. This framework may serve as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for expert interpretation.

title: Early Multisystem Presentation of Frank-ter Haar Syndrome with a Novel Compound Heterozygous SH3PXD2B Variant: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Frank-ter Haar syndrome (FTHS; OMIM #249420) is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic variants in SH3PXD2B, which encodes the podosome adaptor protein TKS4[1]. Fewer than 50 molecularly confirmed cases have been reported. Case presentation: We describe a 6-year-old girl, born at term to non-consanguineous parents, who had low-set ears and craniofacial dysmorphism at birth. A neonatal skull radiograph showed a copper-beaten calvarium, and abdominal ultrasonography incidentally noted bowel-wall thickening; no diagnosis was reached at the time, and echocardiography was normal. At 6 years she presented with global developmental delay, mild intellectual disability, and recurrent lower respiratory tract infections. A repeat skeletal survey confirmed brachycephaly and a persistent copper-beaten skull, with an incidental asymmetry of carpal ossification not previously described in this condition. Paroxysmal inconsolable crying prompted ophthalmological review, which revealed bilateral glaucoma with significant refractive error. Chest radiography and CT thorax were normal. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel missense variant in SH3PXD2B (exon 13; c.2690C>T, p.(Ser897Phe)) in trans with a paternally inherited nonsense variant (c.1219C>T, p.(Arg407*)), confirmed by segregation and consistent with autosomal recessive FTHS. Conclusions: This case expands the mutational spectrum of SH3PXD2B and shows that non-specific neonatal radiological findings may antedate the recognisable FTHS phenotype by years. Paroxysmal crying as the presenting sign of occult glaucoma underscores the need for proactive ophthalmological screening in skeletal dysplasia syndromes. Trial Registration Not applicable.

title: Uncovering neural decisions: How textual interpretation bridges AI and clinical reasoning
abstract: Abstract Medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI) can achieve strong diagnostic performance, yet its decision evidence often remains difficult to verify, raising concerns about reliability and safety in clinical use. Conventional heatmaps mainly localize model-attended lesion regions and have limited capacity to distinguish multiple overlapping clinical features, whereas image-text explanations may describe the image content without being coupled to the actual decision pathway of the target model. Here, we present CRysTal, a neuron-level post-hoc explanation framework that maps decision-related neuronal activations to standardized clinical terminology through two-stage non-negative sparse regression and cross-category fusion. In breast ultrasound diagnosis, CRysTal linked neurons from EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, VGG-19, and ViT-B models to BI-RADS concepts, generating explanations that were more consistent with radiology reports than large-model reasoning, CLIP-Dissect, and linear explanation baselines while preserving the original classification performance. Across the four diagnostic models, CRysTal improved feature-level agreement by 3.4-12.2% and tendency-level agreement by 3.5-19.2% over the second-best baseline. CRysTal further tracked a shift in model explanations during training, from non-specific visual cues toward clinical concepts commonly used by physicians, with concept alignment positively associated with diagnostic performance in ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0 (Pearson r = 0.89 and 0.84, respectively). Its reasoning conflict (RCF) score identified erroneous AI predictions with an AUC of 0.745, outperforming saliency-map-based risk signals (AUC range, 0.542-0.625) and a concept bottleneck model (AUC = 0.643). In a reader study involving 20 ultrasound physicians, CRysTal explanations received mean scores close to 97 for explanation accuracy, readability and guideline concordance, and reduced mean reading time by 10.7% for junior physicians and 4.7% for senior experts. Generalization experiments on external breast ultrasound, thyroid ultrasound and dermoscopy datasets provide initial evidence that CRysTal can support auditable AI explanations across standardized medical imaging terminology systems.

title: Hippocampal surface analysis using discrete Ricci flow and Riemannian metrics for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that is characterized by structural changes of the hippocampus, thus hippocampal morphology becomes an important biomarker for early diagnosis. We propose a geometry-aware framework for AD classification based on discrete Ricci flow and Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) manifold learning. We conformally parameterize the hippocampus surface meshes from the MRI data using Ricci flow and retrieve three geometric descriptors, Heat Kernel Signature, Area Distortion and Conformal Factor, during the Ricci energy optimization process. These features are represented as covariance matrices, resulting in SPD descriptors per subject. To preserve intrinsic manifold structure, classification is performed by KNN with multiple SPD-aware metrics, including the Affine-Invariant Riemannian Metric (AIRM), Wasserstein Metric, Log-Euclidean Metric and so on. Experimental results on ADNI dataset show that AIRM achieves the best performance with 96\% accuracy, which outperforms other metrics evaluated. The results demonstrate that the combination of geometric analysis based on Ricci flow and manifold learning is effective for the diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Complementary Predictive Values of the Glasgow Coma Scale–Pupils Score and Rotterdam CT Score for Outcomes in Adults With Acute Epidural Hematoma and Glasgow Coma Scale of 8 or Lower
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic factors associated with 6-month mortality and functional outcomes in adult patients with severe acute epidural hematoma (AEDH; GCS ≤ 8), focusing on comparing the predictive performance of the Glasgow Coma Scale–Pupils (GCS-P) score and the Rotterdam computed tomography (CT) score. Methods We retrospectively analyzed data from 84 adults with severe AEDH (GCS ≤ 8) registered in the Korean Neurotrauma Data Bank System. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed. For GCS-P score ROC analysis, the analysis direction was set to detect adverse events with lower scores (lower GCS-P values as the positive class) to ensure reproducibility. Paired areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) were compared using DeLong’s test. Results At 6 months, the mortality rate was 22.6% (n = 19), and 40.5% (n = 34) had unfavorable functional outcomes, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE) score of 1–4. In multivariable analysis, the Rotterdam score was an independent predictor of 6-month mortality (OR = 1.972, p = 0.0226), while the GCS-P score was a strong independent predictor of both mortality (OR = 0.660, p = 0.0293) and unfavorable functional outcome (OR = 0.519, p = 0.0002). ROC analysis showed acceptable and comparable mortality prediction for both the Rotterdam score (AUC = 0.759, 95% CI: 0.633–0.872) and GCS-P score (AUC = 0.739, 95% CI: 0.606–0.857; DeLong's p = 0.814). title: Automated Pipeline for Prediction of Spontaneous Paediatric Intracerebral Haemorrhage Outcome Based on CT Images
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for predicting the outcome of spontaneous paediatric intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) by leveraging automatically segmented volumes of total brain (TB), intraparenchymal haemorrhage (IPH), intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH), and perihaematomal oedema (PHE) from cranial CT images in conjunction with clinical data. Methods A retrospective, bi-center study of sICH patients was conducted. The Fudan University Children's Hospital (FUCH) cohort was split 7:3 for training/internal testing, while the Zhejiang University Children’s Hospital (ZUCH) cohort served for external validation. Automated and manual segmentation extracted regions of interest (TB, IPH, IVH, PHE), from which quantitative hematoma volume parameters (e.g., IPH/total brain volume ratio) were derived. Three models were developed: a hematoma location/complication (HLC) model, a hematoma quantification (HQ) model, and a combined model integrating both feature sets. Classifiers (logistic regression, support vector machine, decision tree) were trained with 10-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and decision curve analysis (DCA) on both test sets; SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpreted the combined model. Results Among 147 patients (median age 6.6 years ± 4.28 [SD]; 84 (57.1%) males), 49 (33.3%) had poor outcomes (mRS ≥ 3). Automatic segmentation showed high consistency with radiologists (Dice: IPH 0.837, IVH 0.745; Lin coefficient > 0.8). The combined model outperformed the HLC and HQ models, achieving AUCs of 0.798 (internal) and 0.822 (external). DCA indicated greater clinical net benefit for the combined model across thresholds of 0.10–0.59. The pipeline completed automated segmentation and volume analysis per patient in under 17 seconds. Conclusion The automated pipeline for spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage based on CT images can objectively and accurately predict the outcome of intracerebral haemorrhage in children.

title: Quantifying Data Efficiency in YOLO-Based Femur Segmentation for Axial T1-Weighted MRI
abstract: Abstract Background Automated femur segmentation in T1-weighted MRI is clinically important yet annotation-intensive. Most clinical settings lack the large labelled datasets that conventional deep learning models require. Systematic investigation of how performance scales with training data across architecturally distinct YOLO-family models is currently absent from the literature. Extensive research to surpass the current state of art in terms of segmentation accuracy can improve clinical outcomes by automating femur segmentation in MRI. Methods Three YOLO-family instance segmentation architectures — YOLOv8m-seg, YOLOv11m-seg, and YOLOv26m-seg — were trained across five dataset sizes (N = 40, 100, 200, 400, 800) using a two-phase transfer learning protocol. Forty T1-weighted axial MRI slices of the femur, acquired on a Siemens 3T scanner, were synthetically expanded via an anatomically validated augmentation pipeline. All models were evaluated on a fixed 100-image synthetic test set using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Intersection over Union (IoU), 95th-percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95), Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD), mAP@0.5, and F1 score. Statistical significance was assessed using Mann–Whitney U tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and Cohen’s d effect sizes. Results At N = 800, all three architectures converged to a strong and practically almost indistinguishable performance: YOLOv8m-seg (DSC = 0.960 ± 0.114), YOLOv11m-seg (DSC = 0.963 ± 0.091), and YOLOv26m-seg (DSC = 0.963 ± 0.092); all pairwise Mann–Whitney p > 0.20 with Cohen’s d < 0.03. In the data-scarce regime, YOLOv11m-seg was the only architecture exhibiting monotonically increasing DSC across all conditions, achieving acceptable performance (DSC > 0.87) at N = 100. YOLOv8m-seg collapsed anomalously at N = 100 (DSC = 0.193), and YOLOv26m-seg failed at N = 40 (DSC = 0.163). Inference times were 59–66 ms/image (YOLOv8m-seg), 65–67 ms/image (YOLOv11m-seg), and 70–72 ms/image (YOLOv26m-seg). Conclusions YOLOv11m-seg offers the best balance of data efficiency, segmentation accuracy, and inference speed in the data-scarce regime. YOLO-family models can achieve high segmentation accuracy with as few as 100 annotated slices when transfer learning and anatomically relevant augmentation are applied. Architecture selection is the dominant variable below N = 100 and becomes almost negligible above N = 400.

title: Recurrence of an odontogenic keratocyst in the zygomatic bone with orbital floor involvement: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background An odontogenic keratocyst (OKC) is a benign but locally aggressive intraosseous lesion arising from remnants of the dental lamina or the odontogenic epithelium. It has a marked tendency to recur, and patients with early-stage disease are often asymptomatic; swelling is the most common presenting sign. Involvement of the zygomatic bone and orbital floor is exceptionally rare, since OKC typically arises in the mandibular ramus and molar region. Case presentation 32-year-old woman presented with pain, swelling, and pus discharge below the right eye, with mild orbital dystopia and a scar below the lateral canthus of the right eye. She had a history of multiple surgical procedures for a right maxillary cyst dating back to adolescence. Intraoral examination revealed missing upper right second and third molars and mobility of the premolars. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) demonstrated a well-defined radiolucency involving the infraorbital rim, zygoma, and floor and lateral wall of the right orbit, extending from the maxillary sinus. She underwent cyst enucleation, peripheral ostectomy, and chemical cauterization with modified Carnoy’s solution, together with orbital floor reconstruction using titanium mesh. Histopathology confirmed odontogenic keratocyst. At 7 months’ follow-up there was no clinical or radiological evidence of recurrence, and vision and ocular motility in the operated eye remained unchanged. Conclusions Recurrence of OKC in the zygoma and orbital floor is rare and illustrates how residual satellite cysts left after incomplete removal can reach anatomically inaccessible sites over time. Accurate clinical and radiological diagnosis, combined with enucleation plus an adjunctive measure such as peripheral ostectomy and chemical cauterization, is important to reduce further recurrence, and long-term follow-up remains essential.

title: Giant Pericardial Cyst in the Right Cardiophrenic Angle Mimicking a Hydatid Cyst: A Case Report of a Diagnostic Challenge in an Endemic Region
abstract: Abstract Rationale : Pericardial cysts are rare benign mediastinal lesions, representing approximately 10–20% of all mediastinal masses, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 100,000 persons [1,2]. While most are asymptomatic and discovered incidentally, giant cysts may present with non-specific symptoms mimicking other thoracic pathologies. The majority of pericardial cysts are located in the right cardiophrenic angle (77%) [1,3]. Patient concerns : We report the case of a 57-year-old Syrian male smoker who presented with grade I exertional dyspnea without cough or constitutional symptoms. A chest radiograph performed during routine evaluation revealed a homogeneous density in the right lower lung field. Diagnoses : Chest imaging, including computed tomography (CT), revealed a giant pericardial cyst measuring up to 14.75 cm in greatest dimension, located in the right anterior cardiophrenic angle. The diagnosis was subsequently confirmed by histopathological examination following complete surgical excision. Interventions : The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the pericardial cyst via right posterolateral thoracotomy through the fifth intercostal space, with intraoperative aspiration of clear fluid contents to facilitate safe removal. Outcomes : The patient's symptoms resolved completely following surgical intervention. Chest tube drainage was 500 mL on day 1 and decreased to 80 mL on day 2, with complete lung expansion confirmed radiographically. The chest tube was removed on postoperative day 2, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 3 in stable condition. Follow-up was scheduled at 2 weeks and 2 months postoperatively. Lessons : This case emphasizes the importance of including pericardial cysts in the differential diagnosis of patients with non-specific thoracic symptoms, particularly in regions where echinococcosis is endemic. Elevated anti-echinococcal antibodies (Echinococcus Ab 1/320 positive) initially suggested a hydatid cyst, which was misleading and posed a diagnostic challenge. While video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) is the preferred minimally invasive approach, open thoracotomy remains a safe and effective option for giant cysts with extensive adhesions or challenging anatomical locations [1].

title: A hybrid radiomics–3D CNN model using non-contrast CT for esophagogastric variceal bleeding risk prediction in cirrhosis
abstract: Abstract Background Esophagogastric variceal bleeding (EGVB) is a life-threatening complication of cirrhosis. Non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is free of contrast-related risks, but it cannot directly visualize varices. We therefore developed and validated a fusion model that integrates radiomics with a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D CNN) to predict EGVB risk from NCCT. Methods A total of 137 cirrhotic patients (47 with prior EGVB, 90 without) who underwent NCCT were retrospectively enrolled. Radiomics features (n = 1,919) were extracted from seven ROIs (esophagus, gastric fundus, liver, spleen, portal vein, splenic vein, superior mesenteric vein). For the fusion model, the deep features were concatenated with the LASSO-selected radiomics features from the same training fold. A 3D ResNet-18 CNN learned 128 deep features from the same NCCT volumes. The two feature sets were concatenated and classified by a multilayer perceptron to form the fusion model. Five-fold cross-validation was used for performance evaluation, including AUC, calibration and decision curve analysis. Results The fusion model achieved a mean AUC of 0.884 ± 0.037 across five folds, with a sensitivity of 0.668 and specificity of 0.944 at the Youden-index optimal threshold. The calibration curve showed close agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. Decision curve analysis demonstrated consistent net benefit over both treat-all and treat-none strategies across the threshold range of 0.10–0.50, suggesting potential clinical utility. Conclusions The NCCT-based fusion model integrating radiomics and 3D CNN provides good discrimination and calibration for EGVB risk stratification, and may serve as a non-invasive tool to guide prophylactic decisions. Larger prospective multi-center studies are warranted to confirm its clinical utility.

title: A Rare Case of Breast Cancer with Nasopharyngeal Metastasis: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Although nasopharyngeal metastatic tumors are rare, breast cancer metastasis is uncommon. This report describes a 43-year-old female who developed a nasopharyngeal metastatic lesion after several cycles of breast cancer treatment. She was diagnosed with left breast infiltrating ductal carcinoma (pT2N0M0, Stage II) eight years ago. However, the patient did not undergo standard postoperative adjuvant therapy. She also developed axillary lymph node metastasis during the course of the illness. Although she underwent several systemic treatment cycles, imaging revealed aberrant nasopharyngeal hypertrophy. Endoscopy revealed a single elevated mass within the eustachian tube of the right pharyngeal recess. A pathological biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of breast cancer metastasis. Partial lesion response was achieved on MRIs after administering local intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT, 66 Gy in 33 fractions). The present case underscores the need to be vigilant for atypical metastases during oncological follow-up, as well as the effectiveness of multidisciplinary cooperation in diagnosing and treating such tumors.

title: Qualitative MRI-Based Assessment of Hydrogel Spacer Distribution Predicts Rectal Dosimetry and Acute Toxicity in Prostate Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Hydrogel Rectal Spacers (HRS) are increasingly used to reduce rectal irradiation during stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for localized prostate cancer (PCa). However, the clinical relevance of qualitative spacer distribution remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether MRI-based qualitative characteristics of HRS placement correlate with rectal dosimetry and acute rectal adverse events. Methods This prospective observational study included patients with localized PCa treated with transperineal HRS implantation followed by prostate SBRT between 2023 and 2025. Post-implant T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was used to assess spacer distribution according to three qualitative metrics: Spacer Quality Score (SQS), Symmetry Score (SYM), and Rectal Wall Infiltration score (RWI). Associations between spacer characteristics, rectal dosimetric parameters, and acute rectal toxicity, defined as events occurring within 6 months after SBRT, were analyzed. Results Seventy-six patients were included. Median prostate-rectum separation at the mid-gland level was 10 mm (range, 4–20 mm). SQS was significantly associated with rectal Dmax (p = 0.003), D1cc (p = 0.003), V36Gy (p = 0.018), V30Gy (p = 0.002), and V18Gy (p = 0.002). SYM score correlated with rectal V40Gy (p = 0.009). Acute rectal toxicity occurred in 18 patients (23.7%) and was significantly associated with SQS (p = 0.004). Rectal wall infiltration was identified in 20 patients (26.3%), including edema in 2 (2.6%) and superficial infiltration in 18 (23.7%), but did not correlate with acute rectal adverse events (p = 0.672). Conclusions MRI-based qualitative assessment of HRS distribution provides clinically meaningful information beyond spacer thickness alone. Optimal spacer distribution and symmetry were associated with improved rectal sparing and reduced acute rectal toxicity in patients undergoing prostate SBRT.

title: Segmenting Low-Contrast X-ray Computed Tomography Images of Concrete: An Unsupervised Approach
abstract: Abstract X-Ray Computed Tomography (XCT) is a compelling tool in experimental mechanics, capable of non-destructively extracting information pertaining to the internal morphology of materials. For materials with random heterogeneous morphology such as concrete, such information is of particular relevance since it allows for studies of morphology-related behaviour and for predictive modelling. Nevertheless, XCT images require semantic segmentation for practical usage. Here, concrete poses a unique challenge due to the similar X-ray attenuation coefficients of aggregates and mortar, which result in low contrast between the two phases in the ensuing XCT images. As such, purely intensity-dependent semantic segmentation tools remain unfeasible. While vision transformers (ViTs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are proven techniques for semantic segmentation in such challenging cases, they typically require labelled training data, which is often unavailable for concrete or resource-intensive to obtain, thereby limiting their relevance. To address this challenge, a self-annotation technique is presented here that leverages superpixel algorithms to identify perceptually similar local regions in an image and relates them to the global context by utilizing the receptive field of a CNN-based model. This enables the model to learn a global-local relationship in the images and facilitates the identification of semantically similar structures. When evaluated against manually annotated ground truth on out-of-distribution data, the proposed methodology consistently outperformed direct greyscale thresholding across all pertinent metrics, demonstrating improved discernibility between aggregates and mortar, and providing the most favourable balance of sensitivity and precision for aggregate-phase identification.

Here, concrete poses a unique challenge due to the similar X-ray attenuation coefficients of aggregates and mortar, which result in low contrast between the two phases in the ensuing XCT images. As such, purely intensity-dependent semantic segmentation tools remain unfeasible. While vision transformers (ViTs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are proven techniques for semantic segmentation in such challenging cases, they typically require labelled training data, which is often unavailable for concrete or resource-intensive to obtain, thereby limiting their relevance. To address this challenge, a self-annotation technique is presented here that leverages superpixel algorithms to identify perceptually similar local regions in an image and relates them to the global context by utilizing the receptive field of a CNN-based model. This enables the model to learn a global-local relationship in the images and facilitates the identification of semantically similar structures. When evaluated against manually annotated ground truth on out-of-distribution data, the proposed methodology consistently outperformed direct greyscale thresholding across all pertinent metrics, demonstrating improved discernibility between aggregates and mortar, and providing the most favourable balance of sensitivity and precision for aggregate-phase identification.

title: Clinical and CT radiomics-based differentiation between invasive pulmonary fungal infections and secondary pulmonary tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Background Worldwide diagnoses of invasive pulmonary fungal infection (IPFI) have increased steadily in recent years. Because the clinical manifestations and computed tomography (CT) findings of IPFI frequently resemble those of secondary pulmonary tuberculosis, distinguishing between these two conditions remains challenging and often leads to delayed or incorrect diagnosis. This study was devised with the goal of creating and validating a model for IPFI prediction utilizing clinical and CT radiomics characteristics for distinguishing between IPFI and secondary tuberculosis. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, 153 patients with IPFI and 130 patients with secondary tuberculosis were recruited from two tertiary medical centers between January 1, 2020, and May 31, 2024. Individuals were randomly allocated to training and validation cohorts (7:3). Factors found to be independently predictive of IPFI by multivariable logistic regression were used to establish a clinical model. Radiomics features were selected through variance thresholding, univariate feature selection, and LASSO logistic regression to generate a radiomics score (Rad-score). A combined model including both clinical and radiomics predictors was subsequently developed and compared with the diagnostic performance of junior and senior radiologists. Model discrimination was evaluated via ROC curves, while utility was examined using decision curve analysis. Results Multivariable logistic regression identified long-term broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, hemoglobin concentration, and neutrophil count as independent clinical predictors of IPFI. The Rad-score was derived from 18 radiomics characteristics with non-zero coefficients after selection using LASSO regression. The integrated clinical-radiomics model showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.880 (95% CI, 0.834–0.926) in the training set and 0.844 (95% CI, 0.761–0.926) in the validation set. This model also outperformed both senior and junior radiologists in the validation cohort when distinguishing IPFI from secondary tuberculosis Conclusion A model for IPFI prediction based on clinical and CT-based radiomics characteristics demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for differentiating IPFI from secondary tuberculosis. This approach provides an objective, quantitative tool to facilitate the early identification of IPFI and support clinical decision-making.

title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence-based virtual indigo carmine chromoendoscopy model: a multicenter study
abstract: Abstract Background: Indigo carmine chromoendoscopy (ICC) is an important technique for detecting early gastric and colorectal cancers. However, it is time-consuming and highly dependent on endoscopists experience, limiting its standardized application in clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and systematically evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based virtual ICC model that transforms white light images into virtual ICC images. Methods: This study included 9,174 ICC and 8,403 white light images from 960 cases across five hospitals for model training and testing. A structure-guided multi-step virtual staining generation model based on CycleGAN was developed. Objective metrics for comparing different models included Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Colorfulness Score (CF) with its differential metric ∆CF, and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). Subjective evaluation was conducted by 11 endoscopists (5 seniors, 6 novices) assessing authenticity, contrast, lesion boundary clarity, and microstructural visibility. Results: Our model achieved superior structural fidelity, color representation, and lower FID than comparative models. The accuracy of distinguishing virtual from real images was 78.1% (95% CI: 76.2%–79.9%). No significant differences were observed between virtual and real images in overall contrast (3.85±0.90 vs. 3.92±0.95, P =0.059) and lesion boundary clarity (3.72±0.96 vs. 3.76±0.99, P =0.157). But virtual images scored lower in microstructural visibility (3.35±0.96 vs. 3.61±1.03, P <0.001). Interobserver agreement for virtual images was moderate-to-good (intraclass correlation coefficient>0.5) and comparable to that for real images. No significant interaction effects were observed between staining modality (virtual vs. real) and endoscopists in terms of overall contrast and lesion boundary clarity ( P >0.05). Conclusions: The AI-based virtual ICC model achieved clinically acceptable performance in overall contrast and lesion boundary delineation, with good stability and generalizability. It might reduce reliance on conventional dye-based procedures and improve early gastric and colorectal cancers detection, though prospective real-world validation remains necessary.

title: GlaucoFusionNet: A Causal Inference Aware Multimodal Explainable AI Framework with Counterfactual Reasoning for Glaucoma Risk Prediction
abstract: Abstract Glaucoma is one of a top global cause of irreversible vision loss. But timely diagnosis and thorough risk stratification are the keys to interrupting the progression of blindness. But they are correlation-driven, lack causal reasoning, and provide limited interpretability for clinical decision-making. Furthermore, conventional multimodal approaches are combined retinal imaging and clinical data for diagnosis purpose. But they are not addressing the confounding effects and provide actionable explanations for disease progression. To overcome limitations, study proposes GlaucoFusionNet based on a multimodal explainable AI framework with causal inference for automated glaucoma risk prediction and progression analysis. GlaucoFusionNet is designed for images and tabular data. It integrates retinal fundus images and structured clinical data through a feature fusion architecture. ResNet-based CNN extracts deep retinal image representations. An MLP network model is implemented to accumulate the nonlinear relationships among clinical variables. The extracted embeddings are fused to construct multimodal features for glaucoma classification. SHAP provides feature-level explanation and Grad-CAM visualizes prediction of model on images. Directed Acyclic Graphs used to identify meaningful relationships between clinical factors with reduced spurious correlations. Beyond classification, the framework provides a risk stratification score for identifying high risk patients for disease progression.

title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Explainable Brain Tumour Instance Segmentation and Clinical Report Generation Using ASIO-Optimised YOLO Architectures
abstract: Abstract Automated brain tumour diagnosis using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is essential for rapid oncological intervention, yet conventional deep learning approaches are highly parameter-sensitive and offer limited clinical interpretability. This paper introduces a novel Multi-Agentic Deep Learning Framework for brain tumour detection and classification, developed using the Agent framework. The system orchestrates six specialised Qwen LLM-powered intelligent agents: Data Validation, Preprocessing, Training, Hyperparameter Optimisation, Evaluation, and Explainability/Reporting. To maximise diagnostic precision, we integrate state-of-the-art real-time detectors—YOLOv8, YOLOv11, and YOLO26 — with the Asteroid Satellite-Inspired optimisation (ASIO) metaheuristic to dynamically evolve hyperparameters, including learning rate, batch size, and confidence thresholds. Experimental evaluations conducted on a publicly available brain MRI dataset demonstrate that ASIO optimisation yields substantial performance improvements over baseline methods. Specifically, the ASIO-optimised YOLO26 model achieved a peak mean Average Precision (mAP@50) of 0.9321, a box precision of 0.9651, and a recall of 0.8851, outperforming the baseline YOLO26 detector (mAP@50 of 0.8407), as well as the optimised YOLOv8 (mAP@50 of 0.8451) and YOLOv11 (mAP@50 of 0.7751) variants. Furthermore, the integration of Qwen-powered agents enables automated, natural-language diagnostic reasoning and real-time report generation directly from inference metrics, while achieving a rapid inference latency of less than 15 milliseconds per slice. By unifying automated hyperparameter evolution with LLM-based clinical report generation, the proposed multi-agentic framework minimises manual diagnostic latency and establishes a highly transparent, explainable decision-support tool suitable for real-world clinical neuro-radiology workflows.

title: Choroid plexus volume in relation to volumetric and susceptibility characteristics of white matter hyperintensities in metabolic syndrome: a two-cohort MRI study
abstract: Abstract Aims This study aims to explore the pathophysiological links among MetS, choroid plexus (CP), and white matter hyperintensities (WMHs) to clarify mechanisms of cognitive decline in MetS. Methods A total of 133 participants from the Jinan cohort and 5,594 from the UK Biobank (UKB) were included. In Jinan, a three-way interaction (CP volume × WMH susceptibility × MetS) was modeled for WMH volume. Multivariate regression, restricted cubic spline, and generalized estimating equations assessed CP-WMH associations. Mediation analyses evaluated whether WMH mediated links between MetS severity and cognitive domains. In the UKB, serial mediation analyses using structural equation models were performed to test the directional cascade from triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index to cognitive domains. Results CP volume correlated with WMH characteristics across both cohorts. In Jinan, the association of CP and WMH was significant only in MetS individuals with elevated WMH susceptibility. Longitudinally, CP volume showed a time-varying negative association with WMH susceptibility. In the UKB, both total WMH and periventricular hyperintensity (PVH) volume increased with CP over time. WMH volume was linked to poorer processing speed and global cognition and mediated the association between MetS severity and cognition in the UKB. And significant indirect effects of TyG on global cognition via CP and WMH volume was found in the UKB. Conclusion MetS was associated with CP enlargement and WMH abnormalities across two cohorts. These imaging characteristics were further associated with poorer processing speed and global cognitive performance.

title: Morphological Variations of the Nasopalatine Canal and Incisive Foramen Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Variations in the morphology and dimensions of the NPC and incisive foramen may influence surgical procedures such as implant placement, orthognathic surgery, and other interventions performed in the premaxillary region. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) provides accurate three-dimensional evaluation of these anatomical structures. This study aimed to evaluate the frequency of different anatomical types of the nasopalatine canal and incisive foramen and their related factors using CBCT images in Iranian Population. Materials and Methods This analytical cross-sectional study evaluated 180 CBCT images (90 males, 90 females) from patients referred to the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology, Faculty of Dentistry, Islamic Azad University of Tehran. Sagittal, axial, and coronal sections were used to assess NPC dimensions, curvature, angular orientation, and incisive foramen morphology. Data were analyzed using Chi-square and independent sample t-tests. Results The most common anatomical type of the nasopalatine canal was Type A in both genders. No significant association was found between canal morphology and gender. The round shape was the most frequent form of the incisive foramen in both males and females. Significant differences were observed between males and females regarding the anteroposterior (p = 0.003) and mediolateral diameters of the incisive foramen (p = 0.041) (p < 0.05). Conclusion Considerable anatomical variations exist in the morphology and dimensions of the nasopalatine canal and incisive foramen. Accurate CBCT evaluation before surgical procedures in the anterior maxillary region is strongly recommended to minimize complications and improve treatment planning.

title: Cryptogenic Near-Complete Left Internal Carotid Artery Occlusion in a 20-Year-Old Male: A Diagnostic and Pharmacological Challenge.
abstract: Abstract Background Large vessel occlusions (LVO), particularly those involving the internal carotid artery (ICA), are exceedingly rare in young adults. These events typically prompt aggressive screening for underlying prothrombotic and metabolic disorders. Case presentation A 20-year-old male presented with severe headache, slurred speech, right-sided seizures, and hemiplegia. Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) identified a near-complete occlusion of the intracranial segments of the left ICA. Despite the severe cerebrovascular event, comprehensive screening for metabolic and hypercoagulability factors remained unremarkable, which notably included a strictly normal baseline serum homocysteine level of 6.67 µmol/L. The patient was successfully managed with aggressive dual antithrombotic therapy alongside empirical folic acid supplementation. During regular clinical follow-ups every 2 months over a 2-year period, the patient demonstrated significant neurological recovery without any recurrent ischemic events. Conclusion This case underscores the diagnostic challenges associated with cryptogenic LVOs in young adults. It emphasizes the likelihood of spontaneous arterial dissection when metabolic anomalies are absent. Furthermore, the case discusses the pharmacological rationale for utilizing empirical metabolic interventions in cases of unexplained early-onset stroke.

title: Correlation between Alvarado Score and Measurement of Appendiceal Wall Thickness and Intraluminal Lumen Thickness on CT in the Diagnosis of Acute Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Background Acute appendicitis remains the most common abdominal surgical emergency. Computed tomography (CT) is progressively used for diagnosis, yet the optimal CT parameters and their correlation with clinical scoring systems such as the Alvarado score remain incompletely characterized. Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of appendiceal wall thickness and intraluminal lumen thickness on contrast-enhanced CT for the diagnosis of acute appendicitis, determine optimal cut-off values by ROC curve analysis, and to correlate the Alvarado score with the CT findings. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study of 71 patients with clinically suspected acute appendicitis who underwent contrast-enhanced CT at a tertiary referral center (January 2024–January 2026). Appendiceal outer-to-outer diameter, lumen thickness and wall thickness were assessed by two independent radiologists. Alvarado scores were stratified into low (1–3), intermediate (4–7), and high (8–10) risk groups. ROC curve analysis was calculated to identify optimal diagnostic cut-off values. Results Sixty-three cases (88.7%) were surgically confirmed as acute appendicitis. Periappendiceal fat stranding was present in all confirmed-positive cases (100%). ROC analysis identified optimal cut-offs of 6.6 mm for outer diameter (AUC 0.875; sensitivity 87.9%, specificity 100%), 1.5 mm for wall thickness (AUC 0.876; sensitivity 82.3%, specificity 84.5%), and 2.21 mm for lumen thickness (AUC 0.903; sensitivity 95.6%, specificity 68.0%). All intermediate- and high-risk Alvarado groups showed CT-confirmed appendicitis rates of ≥ 93.8%. Conclusion Appendiceal lumen thickness at a cut-off of 2.21 mm achieved the highest AUC (0.903) for the CT diagnosis of acute appendicitis, with higher sensitivity to the conventional outer-diameter criterion. Combined assessment of CT parameters with the Alvarado score improves diagnostic stratification and may reduce unnecessary surgical intervention.

title: Computational aberration-corrected volumetric imaging of single retinal cell dynamics in the living eye
abstract: Abstract The eye offers a unique non-invasive window for accessing single-cell level structures and functions of the central nervous system (CNS) throughout the retina. However, strong, space-varying ocular aberrations and limited volumetric imaging speed challenges large-scale single-cell imaging in living eyes. Here, we present plenoptic illumination scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (PI-SLO), a 3D fluorescence retinal imaging modality that enables high-speed, widefield, volumetric single-cell imaging with low phototoxicity. By capturing multiple angular views of fluorescence signals from the entire retinal volume, PI-SLO performs digital aberration correction and reconstructs 3D images over a >20° field of view at >23 volume per second. We apply PI-SLO to investigate three key aspects of CNS physiology through the living mouse retina: microglial process dynamics, vascular perfusion, and light-evoked calcium activity in inner retinal neurons. PI-SLO provides a versatile, non-invasive platform for studying vision, retinal disease, and CNS physiology at cellular resolution.

title: Bilateral Acute Retinal Necrosis Complicated by Concurrent Neuroborreliosis in an Immunocompromised Patient: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Purpose To report a case of bilateral acute retinal necrosis (ARN) with an atypical and incomplete initial treatment response, which prompted an extended systemic investigation ultimately revealing a concurrent, previously undiagnosed neuroborreliosis in an immunocompromised patient. Methods A 50-year-old immunocompromised woman, with a background of abdominal desmoid tumor, and Sulfasalazine-treated rheumatoid arthritis (RA), presented with unilateral visual deterioration, pain, and photophobia, preceded by three weeks of headache and fatigue. Bilateral ARN was diagnosed on clinical grounds and confirmed by vitreous PCR following diagnostic pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) of the left eye. Standard antiviral therapy with Valacyclovir was promptly initiated, supplemented by oral Prednisone three days later. Given the insufficient and asymmetric treatment response, with paradoxical worsening of the right eye despite ongoing therapy, an urgent systemic infectious workup was conducted in collaboration with the department of infectious diseases, including brain MRI, lumbar puncture, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis. Results Vitreous PCR confirmed varicella-zoster virus (VZV) as the causative pathogen of the ARN. However, the suboptimal clinical response to combined antiviral and corticosteroid therapy raised suspicion of an additional co-existing infectious process. CSF analysis revealed elevated intrathecal IgM and IgG antibodies against Borrelia burgdorferi, establishing a diagnosis of active neuroborreliosis. Following the addition of targeted systemic antibiotic therapy, a marked clinical improvement was observed, with arrest of retinal necrosis and resolution of vitritis in both eyes. Despite this, the left eye subsequently developed a total retinal detachment. Conclusion This case underscores that an incomplete or paradoxical response to antiviral and corticosteroid therapy in ARN should prompt a thorough systemic infectious workup. title: Clinicopathological Determinants of Prognosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Integrating Histopathology with an IHC-Based Molecular Subclassification
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy that has undergone major therapeutic changes over the last two decades. Here, a real-world clinicopathological cohort integrating morphology, prognostic parameters, immunohistochemical surrogate markers for molecular stratification, and treatment outcome data is presented. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center study of 597 patients with histologically confirmed HCC (or occasional cases of combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) diagnosed at the Institute of Pathology, University of Regensburg, between 2000 and 2024. Clinical, pathological, laboratory, and follow-up data were merged with regional cancer registry data. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression. In a tissue microarray-based subcohort, immunohistochemistry for p53, Cyclin A2, Cyclin E1, β-catenin, and L-FABP1 was evaluated as a surrogate for a recently proposed molecular subclassification. Systemic treatment response and progression-free survival were assessed in patients with available follow-up data. Results The cohort comprised 486 men and 111 women, with a median age at diagnosis of 70 years in men and 67 years in women. Cirrhosis (49.7%), viral hepatitis (24.0%), diabetes mellitus (33.8%), arterial hypertension (45.2%), and steatosis hepatis (24.3%) were frequent background conditions. Median overall survival was 52 months. Survival declined with increasing grade and with incomplete resection. In multivariate Cox regression, older age, advanced T category, vascular invasion, positive resection margins, poor differentiation, macrotrabecular-massive (MTM) subtype, absence of tumor capsule, steatosis, and elevated alkaline phosphatase showed prognostic relevance, with age, T category, vascular invasion, resection status, MTM subtype, tumor capsule, and alkaline phosphatase emerging as particularly robust predictors. In the tissue microarray cohort, p53-high expression was independently associated with worse overall survival, whereas combined Cyclin A2/E1 high expression was significant in univariate analysis. L-FABP1 loss and nuclear β-catenin accumulation were not associated with outcome. Patients treated with atezolizumab/bevacizumab showed higher response rates than those treated with sorafenib. Conclusions This quarter-century single-center study highlights the multifactorial background, morphological diversity, and prognostic heterogeneity of HCC in routine clinical practice. Established clinicopathological variables remain the strongest determinants of survival, while p53 immunohistochemistry may provide additional prognostic information as an accessible molecular surrogate. The data further reflect the changing systemic treatment landscape from sorafenib to immunotherapy-based regimens in a real-world cohort.

title: Medical imaging in Bothrops lanceolatus envenomation: a retrospective series from Martinique
abstract: Abstract Background: Bothrops lanceolatus (Bl), a pit viper endemic to Martinique, is responsible for 40–50 envenomations annually. These are characterized by systemic thrombotic complications, that can lead to cerebral, myocardial, or pulmonary infarction. The introduction of the specific antivenom Bothrofav has substantially improved patient prognosis and management. Although severity grading remains primarily clinical, the specific role of medical imaging in this setting is underexplored. We aimed to delineate the contribution of imaging to the management of B. lanceolatus envenomation. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study at the University Hospital of Martinique from January 2011 to August 2024. All patients with documented B. lanceolatus envenomation were included. We collected data in imaging use, clinical severity grade, and complications. Bivariate analyses were performed to examine associations between clinical status and imaging use. Results: A total of 389 patients were included (median age 48 years [IQR 35–59]; 128 [33%] women). Seventy-nine patients (20%) underwent at least one imaging examination, for a total of 127 studies. Imaging was infrequently used in mild envenomation (Grades 1–2) but significantly more frequent in severe cases (Grades 3–4, p < 0.01) and then complications were present, including compartment syndrome, shock, coma, infection, or the need for surgery. Eleven thrombotic events were confirmed in six pa three cerebral infarctions, three myocardial infarctions, two pulmonary embolisms, and three deep vein thromboses. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) and Doppler ultrasound were central to the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism and peripheral thrombosis, respectively. Conclusions: Although the management of snakebite envenomation remains primarily clinical, judicious use of medical imaging, specifically CT, MRI, and Doppler ultrasound, serves as a valuable adjunct. Imaging enhances severity grading and is essential for confirming thrombotic complications, thereby supporting the development of standardized, imaging-based management protocols for B. lanceolatus envenomation.

title: Determinants of Access to Brain Tumor Care in Angola: A Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Background. Brain tumors require an exceptionally demanding continuum of care because clinical outcomes depend on timely recognition, neuroimaging, neurosurgical decision-making, pathology, oncology, radiotherapy, supportive treatment, and longitudinal follow-up. In low- and middle-income settings, this pathway is commonly disrupted by delays, out-of-pocket costs, urban concentration of services, and weak referral systems. Objective. To map the determinants of access to brain tumor care in Angola and to situate the Angolan context within the broader sub-Saharan African literature, with emphasis on clinical recognition, access to computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), neurosurgery, pathology, oncology, radiotherapy, financing, geography, continuity of care, and clinical governance. Methods. We conducted an exploratory scoping review of published and documentary sources, guided by PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. Indexed literature, African regional sources, clinical guidance documents, and institutional materials with analytic relevance to Angola were synthesized narratively according to major domains of access. Results. International and regional evidence indicates that brain tumor care is vulnerable to serial bottlenecks, including delayed presentation, initially nonspecific symptoms, diagnostic confusion with stroke, central nervous system infection, or epilepsy, inconsistent access to CT and MRI, specialist shortages, delayed surgery, limited pathology capacity, inadequate radiotherapy availability, and loss to follow-up. In Angola, disease-specific published evidence remains scarce, and the exact patient profile and care timelines are still insufficiently documented. Nevertheless, regional African literature and the minimum requirements of neuro-oncology suggest that access in Angola depends less on any single technical intervention than on the coordinated functioning of the entire diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conclusions. Access to brain tumor treatment in Angola should be framed as a systemic neuro-oncology challenge. Priority actions include strengthening clinical suspicion and referral pathways, ensuring functional CT and MRI access, protecting neurosurgical and anesthetic capacity, improving reliable pathology, integrating care with oncology and radiotherapy, expanding financial protection, and creating clinical registries capable of measuring delays, treatments, and outcomes.

title: Disease Spectrum Analysis and AI-Assisted Screening of Fundus Disorders Using Portable Handheld Fundus Imaging in Health Examination Populations
abstract: Abstract Objective: Portable handheld fundus imaging facilitates convenient population‑based eye screening, yet its clinical application is hindered by unstable image quality and insufficient real‑world population disease evidence. This study aimed to establish a feasible screening workflow for handheld fundus photography in physical examination cohorts, combining standardized image quality management, population fundus disease spectrum analysis, and intelligent auxiliary disease identification to support large‑scale eye health screening. Methods: A total of 58,500 non‑mydriatic handheld fundus images were consecutively collected from a tertiary general hospital health examination center between 2020 and 2025. Automated standardized quality assessment was performed to screen valid images for subsequent analyses. Qualified high‑quality images were included to analyze the distribution characteristics of fundus diseases in the general population. Meanwhile, a two‑stage intelligent auxiliary screening strategy was implemented to identify abnormal fundus images and further categorize specific types of abnormal fundus diseases. The screening and classification performance of multiple deep learning networks was comprehensively benchmarked on handheld fundus data. Results: The overall fundus abnormality rate of high‑quality images was 32.22%. Myopia‑related fundus changes (19.84%), retinal vascular diseases (5.89%), and macular diseases (3.82%) were the predominant abnormal fundus diseases in the examined population. Distinct age‑related distribution differences were observed: younger individuals were mainly affected by myopia‑related changes, whereas elderly populations had a higher burden of vascular and macular diseases. The established intelligent system achieved favorable performance in fundus abnormality screening (AUC = 0.9612) and fine‑grained abnormal disease classification (macro‑AUC = 0.8445). Lightweight models achieved favorable performance in handheld fundus image analysis. Retinal foundation models, pre‑trained on conventional adult fundus datasets, showed limited performance advantages in this portable imaging scenario. Conclusion: Standardized quality control and intelligent auxiliary analysis may support large‑scale multi‑disease fundus screening using portable handheld imaging in routine physical examinations. The observed age‑stratified distribution pattern of fundus diseases in this health examination population provides real‑world evidence for portable fundus screening. This study presents a practical framework for population‑level fundus health surveillance.

title: Comparison of One-Hole Split Endoscopy and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy for Far-Lateral Lumbar Disc Herniation at L5/S1: A Short-Term Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes between One-hole Split Endoscopy (OSE) and Unilateral Biportal Endoscopy (UBE) for L5/S1 far-lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH). Methods This retrospective study included 47 patients with L5-S1 FLLDH (July 2022-July 2024) divided into OSE and UBE groups. Surgical outcomes were documented. Radiographic parameters—including intervertebral foramen area (IVFA), height of the superior articular process (HSAP), lumbosacral lordotic angle (LLA), sagittal translation (ST), and disc height (DH)—were compared between groups. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and Macnab criteria. Results Both groups exhibited significant improvement in VAS and ODI scores at all postoperative time points (P < 0.05), with no significant differences between groups. Excellent-to-good rates were 91.3% for OSE and 91.7% for UBE. One dural tear occurred in the OSE group. No significant intergroup differences were observed in any radiographic parameter. Postoperative ST and LLA remained stable (P > 0.05), whereas DH decreased, IVFA increased, and HSAP decreased (all P < 0.05). The UBE group demonstrated shorter operative time, while the OSE group had smaller incisions and less intraoperative blood loss. Conclusion Both UBE and OSE are effective minimally invasive approaches for treating L5-S1 FLLDH.

title: A Case Report and Literature Review of Extraskeletal Osteosarcoma of the Abdominal Wall
abstract: Abstract Background Extraskeletal osteosarcoma (ESOS) is a rare form of soft-tissue cancer characterized by the formation of osteoid matrix, bone, and cartilage. The clinical diagnosis has not been easy, and the prognosis is usually bad, with significant local recurrence rates and metastasis at a distance. The occurrence of ESOS in the abdominal wall is extremely uncommon. Case presentation: We present the case of a 60-year-old male who developed an enlarging mass in the lower right abdominal wall over 6 months with a local bulge and erythema, but without severe pain. Physical examination revealed a hard, non-tender mass measuring approximately 6 x 6 cm with indistinct margins but good mobility. Superficial ultrasonography indicated a primarily solid mass 59 x 53 x 39 mm. The operation was performed using wide surgical excision with general anesthesia. Intraoperative frozen section pathology revealed a mesenchymal soft tissue tumor, and this was confirmed by definitive histopathology with immunohistochemistry as ESOS. It is important to note that after surgery, the patient revealed that he had a history of thymoma, which had been treated with radiotherapy five years earlier; however, this information was initially not given. After surgery, the patient was given four courses of chemotherapy (cisplatin and ifosfamide) and radiation therapy. At 12-month follow-up, the surgical wound was well-healed, with no signs of local recurrence or new metastatic lesions. Conclusions Conclusively, ESOS of the abdominal wall is an uncommon and very malignant disease that tends to be misdiagnosed because of its non-specific clinical manifestations. This case demonstrates the significance of the extensive history-taking process, histopathological assessment with immunohistochemistry, and multimodal intervention approaches. The patient's prior radiotherapy underscores the need for a thorough clinical examination. This report adds to the sparse literature on ESOS of the abdomen and guides planning, early diagnosis, and treatment.

title: The AI-CDSS Evidence Gap: A Critical Analysis of Outcome Measurement, Human-AI Interaction, and Implementation Validation
abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) are increasingly promoted to improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making. However, questions remain about whether current evidence adequately demonstrates meaningful patient benefit. Existing research relies heavily on surrogate diagnostic metrics, provides limited insight into clinician–AI interaction, and rarely evaluates implementation in real-world healthcare settings. This review synthesizes evidence across these interconnected domains to identify critical gaps in AI-CDSS evaluation. Methods: A critical narrative review was conducted using the Grant and Booth (2009) review typology and thematic narrative synthesis. Literature published between January 2015 and May 2026 was searched in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and IEEE Xplore using three domains: clinical effectiveness, human–AI interaction, and implementation science. Relevant regulatory guidance and evaluation frameworks were identified through targeted searches of institutional and professional organization websites. Results: The search identified 1,247 records; following screening and eligibility assessment, 33 sources (28 peer-reviewed publications and five grey literature documents) were included. The strongest effectiveness evidence, a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomized controlled trials involving 12,657 participants, demonstrated only a small pooled effect (standardized mean difference 0.182; 95% CI 0.003–0.362; GRADE: moderate), with all trials measuring diagnostic accuracy rather than patient-centred outcomes such as mortality or length of stay. Most studies originated from East Asia and focused on radiology, limiting generalizability. Human factors evidence identified significant vulnerabilities, including automation bias that reduced diagnostic accuracy among inexperienced radiologists when incorrect AI recommendations were presented, high false-positive alarm rates promoting alert fatigue, and limited clinician scrutiny of erroneous AI outputs. Although evaluation and implementation frameworks, including CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, CFIR, and RE-AIM, have been developed, prospective validation remains limited, with almost no implementation evidence from sub-Saharan Africa or other low- and middle-income countries. Conclusion: Current AI-CDSS evidence inadequately captures real-world effectiveness and unintended harms. Future research should prioritize patient-centred outcomes, rigorous evaluation of clinician–AI interaction, and prospective validation of implementation frameworks across diverse healthcare settings. Strengthening evidence standards, including fairness and equity considerations, is essential for the safe, effective, and scalable deployment of AI-CDSS.

title: Low-Dose Esketamine Combined with Propofol for Sedation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Bidirectional Endoscopy: A single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
abstract: Abstract Background Sedation for same-visit bidirectional gastrointestinal endoscopy in elderly patients remains a major clinical challenge. Propofol monotherapy carries a prominent risk of respiratory and circulatory depression, particularly in geriatric patients with limited physiological reserve. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, exerts sympathomimetic effects that may offset propofol-induced hypotension and hypoxaemia. However, high-quality clinical evidence in this specific population is insufficient. This trial evaluated whether low-dose esketamine added to propofol reduces cardiopulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing bidirectional endoscopy. Methods In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, 316 elective patients aged 60–80 years with ASA physical status I–III were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive either intravenous esketamine 0.15 mg/kg or normal saline placebo, followed by propofol 1 mg/kg for sedation induction. The dual primary outcomes were the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia. Prespecified secondary outcomes included procedural efficiency and quality indicators. Results The overall incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxaemia showed no significant intergroup differences. However, patients in the esketamine group maintained more stable intraoperative systolic blood pressure (SBP) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SPO₂) throughout the procedure. Esketamine also demonstrated superior procedural efficiency: shorter median induction time (120 s vs. 140 s; P < 0.001), 16.7% lower median propofol consumption (125 mg vs. 150 mg; P < 0.001), and 100% first-attempt gastroscope insertion success versus 94.9% with placebo (P = 0.007). Intraoperative bucking was halved (6.3% vs. 13.9%; P = 0.039). These gains were not offset by increased adverse events, including psychotomimetic effects, nausea and vomiting, dizziness, or cognitive impairment. Recovery times and patient satisfaction remained similarly high. Conclusions In conclusion, adjuvant low-dose esketamine combined with propofol did not reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension or hypoxemia in elderly patients undergoing same-visit bidirectional endoscopy. However, intraoperative SBP and SpO₂ were better preserved in patients receiving esketamine during the whole procedure. This regimen provided multiple clinical benefits including shortened induction time, higher first-pass gastroscopy insertion success rate, lower propofol dosage and reduced intraoperative bucking, without increasing overall adverse event risks. Trial registration Trial registration: This trial was prospectively registered on 26 March 2025 in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (registration number ChiCTR2500099643; https://www.chictr.org.cn/).

title: Lichen Sclerosus, Breast Cancer, and the Impact of Hormonal Therapy: A Large-Scale Propensity-Matched Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate the bidirectional association between lichen sclerosus and breast cancer, and to assess whether hormonal breast cancer therapies influence the subsequent risk of developing lichen sclerosus. Methods: This retrospective cohort study utilized a global electronic health record network containing over 204 million patients. Female patients with lichen sclerosus were compared to matched controls with postmenopausal atrophic vaginitis. Reciprocally, breast cancer patients were compared to matched controls who underwent mammography without a cancer diagnosis. Cohorts were propensity-score matched for age, race, ethnicity, body mass index, and smoking status. Results: Among 77,386 patients with lichen sclerosus and 77,163 controls, lichen sclerosus was associated with a lower incidence of subsequent breast cancer (2.22% vs. 2.55%; RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.82-0.93, p<0.001). Conversely, in 563,498 breast cancer patients without hormonal therapy versus 563,676 controls, breast cancer was associated with a higher incidence of subsequent lichen sclerosus (0.18% vs. 0.10%; RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.67-2.04, p<0.001). Hormonal therapy exposure in breast cancer patients showed a minimal risk increase for lichen sclerosus (RR 1.07, p=0.031), with no significant association found for tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors specifically. Conclusion: Lichen sclerosus is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, whereas breast cancer is associated with a higher subsequent incidence of lichen sclerosus. Because this increased risk persists in patients who did not receive hormonal therapy, mechanisms beyond estrogen deprivation likely drive the development of lichen sclerosus in breast cancer patients.

title: Extreme Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor–Associated Thrombocytosis with Concurrent C-MET Upregulation Evolution in Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) carries a dismal prognosis. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have modestly improved survival, but durable responses are uncommon, and hematologic immune-related adverse events (irAEs)—<1% of treated patients—remain poorly characterised. Extreme reactive thrombocytosis (> 1,000 × 10⁹/L) has not been documented during ICI therapy for ES-SCLC, and its mechanism and management are undefined. Endocrine irAEs (secondary adrenal insufficiency) are increasingly recognised, but their concurrence with hematologic toxicity has not been described. Case Presentation. A 62-year-old man with ES-SCLC received first-line Toripalimab-based immunotherapy. On day 71 (24 February 2026), the platelet count peaked at 1,033 × 10⁹/L, prompting urgent therapeutic plateletpheresis. Concurrent serology showed interferon-γ approximately 45 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), ferritin approximately 20× ULN, and elevated soluble interleukin-2 receptor, consistent with an incomplete hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) phenotype. C-reactive protein peaked at 178.40 mg/L and interleukin-6 reached 199.68 pg/mL on 2 March 2026, supporting cytokine-driven myeloproliferation. Serial tumor biopsies documented C-MET evolution from 10% weak-positive to 80% strong-positive. Early tumor shrinkage (11% reduction from a 118-mm baseline) coincided with the platelet peak on day 71, while maximal radiographic response (50% reduction) was achieved on day 121 (15 April 2026). Treatment was modified with antiangiogenic optimization (Anlotinib 12 mg daily) and Toripalimab was substituted with Tislelizumab. Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (PTV 45 Gy/25 fractions, PGTV 50 Gy/25 fractions, simultaneous integrated boost) commenced on 23 May 2026. On the same day, endocrinology consultation confirmed secondary adrenal insufficiency (ACTH < 0.22 pmol/L, cortisol < 2.76 nmol/L), managed with prednisolone replacement and blood pressure restoration. Conclusions. The temporal sequence—peak platelet count (day 71) preceding maximal tumor response (day 121) implicates immune activation, not tumor burden, as the thrombocytosis driver. C-MET upregulation under PD-1 blockade may represent both a resistance mechanism and a targetable salvage pathway. This first reported concurrence of extreme thrombocytosis, incomplete HLH, and secondary adrenal insufficiency in a single ES-SCLC patient underscores the need for multi-system irAE monitoring. Trial Registration Clinical trial number: not applicable. This is a retrospective single-patient case report; no prospective clinical trial was conducted, and no patient was enrolled in a registered clinical trial for the treatments described.

title: Prediction of LN-prRLN Metastasis in cN0 PTMC Patients Using Logistic Regression and Machine Learning: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background The incidence of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) is steadily increasing, with metastasis to lymph nodes posterior to the right recurrent laryngeal nerve (LN-prRLN) occurring in 7.1% to 34.9% of cases. Preoperative ultrasound fails to detect most LN-prRLN metastases. Accurate risk assessment of LN-prRLN in clinically node-negative (cN0) PTMC patients is essential for determining the appropriate surgical extent and evaluating the feasibility of active surveillance. Objective To develop and compare logistic regression and machine learning models for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients, thereby supporting individualized preoperative and intraoperative clinical decision-making. Methods A total of 1051 cN0 PTMC patients were retrospectively analyzed and randomly allocated to training and validation sets at a 7:3 ratio. Clinical, ultrasonographic, and pathological variables were collected. Using LN-prRLN metastasis status as the endpoint, logistic regression and multiple machine learning models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), calibration curves, and precision-recall curves. The best-performing machine learning model was compared with the logistic model, and SHAP values were employed for model interpretability. Results Multivariate logistic regression identified anterior prelaryngeal lymph node metastatic ratio (LNMR) and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR as independent predictors of LN-prRLN metastasis. Among machine learning algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the best discriminative ability and calibration stability. Although XGBoost yielded higher area under the ROC curve (AUC) values than the logistic model in both training and validation sets, the difference was not statistically significant. SHAP analysis revealed that anterior prelaryngeal LNMR and anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve LNMR were the two most influential predictors, contributing cumulatively over 66% to the prediction with strong interaction effects. Other notable contributors included anterior recurrent laryngeal nerve lymph node metastasis, prelaryngeal lymph node metastasis, tumor size, left central compartment LNMR, capsular invasion, age, left central compartment lymph node metastasis, and multifocality. Conclusion Both logistic regression and machine learning models are reliable tools for predicting LN-prRLN metastasis in cN0 PTMC patients. Integrating these models can assist clinicians in accurately identifying high-risk patients preoperatively or intraoperatively, enabling more patient-centered clinical decisions.

title: OCT evaluation as a prognostic indicator for management of macular edema secondary to venous occlusion treated with Ranibizumab
abstract: Abstract Aim: To study OCT characteristics as a prognostic guide in macular edema secondary to non-ischemic central retinal vein occlusion treated with intravitreal Ranibizumab Materials and methods: 60 patients with macular edema secondary to non-ischemic central retinal vein occlusion treated with Ranibizumab OCT analyzed on pattern of macular edema, reflectivity of outer band of photoreceptor-RPE complex. Its bearing on visual prognosis was analyzed. RESULTS: Good reflectivity of outer layer is a good prognostic feature. Cystoid pattern is a better prognostic indicator than sub retinal fluid Conclusion: The type of macular edema and reflectivity of third high reflectivity band before treatment can be predictive of visual outcome

title: A Simplified Surgical Bypass for Complete Afferent Loop Obstruction After Pancreaticoduodenectomy Guided by Afferent Loop Length: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Recurrent afferent loop obstruction (ALO) after pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is a challenging clinical problem. When tumor recurrence leads to complete occlusion with failure of guidewire passage, endoscopic interventions are rarely successful. Although percutaneous transhepatic cholangial drainage (PTCD) can provide emergency decompression, it requires permanent external drainage, leading to digestive fluid loss and decreased quality of life. While surgical bypass is a recognized principle, the anatomical prerequisites that determine its feasibility—particularly the available length of the proximal afferent loop—have not been systematically addressed. This report aims to fill this gap by proposing an experience-based reference for patient selection based on loop length and presenting long-term quality-of-life data. Case Presentation: A 72-year-old male developed complete ALO due to pancreatic cancer recurrence 7 months after PD. Preoperative assessment showed a single-site obstruction and a sufficiently long proximal afferent loop (>50 cm, intraoperative estimation), which enabled a direct, tension-free side-to-side anastomosis between the proximal afferent loop and the distal jejunum without Roux-en-Y reconstruction. Results: Symptoms resolved within 48 hours postoperatively. Total bilirubin decreased from 156 μmol/L to 34 μmol/L by postoperative day 7. GIQLI score increased from 28 preoperatively to 52 at 3 months. No recurrent obstruction occurred during 6-month follow-up. The patient died 9 months postoperatively due to widespread metastases. Conclusion: For carefully selected patients with complete recurrent ALO after PD in whom endoscopy is not feasible, afferent loop jejunal anastomosis appears safe and effective. Based on our experience, a proximal afferent loop length >50 cm and a single-site obstruction are favorable anatomical conditions allowing simplified direct anastomosis without complex Roux-en-Y reconstruction. However, these criteria represent a single-surgeon experience and require validation in larger cohorts.
