title: Impact of AI-assisted chest radiography on clinical decision-making: A temporal analysis of CT referral rates and the proportion of positive CT in cardiology outpatient setting
abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into chest radiography (CXR) interpretation to assist in the detection of pulmonary abnormalities. However, whether AI-assisted interpretation influences subsequent clinical decision-making in routine practice remains unclear. We investigated the association between the implementation of AI-assisted CXR interpretation and subsequent clinical decision-making, focusing on chest computed tomography (CT) referral and the detection of clinically relevant pulmonary abnormalities in a cardiology outpatient setting. Methods: We retrospectively identified adult patients who underwent CXR at their first visit to a cardiology outpatient department between March 2020 and February 2024. A commercially available AI system was routinely applied to CXR examinations throughout the study period. Patients were divided into two consecutive periods according to the date of CXR acquisition, and temporal trends were additionally evaluated by acquisition year. The primary outcome was referral for chest CT within 30 days after CXR, and the secondary outcome was the proportion of CT referrals resulting in positive findings. Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) incorporating cardiologist-level random effects were used to evaluate temporal changes in CT referral and positive CT findings. Results: A total of 9279 patients were included, comprising 5320 patients in the earlier period and 3959 in the later period. The CT referral rate was significantly higher in the later period than in the earlier period. In GLMM analysis, the likelihood of CT referral increased significantly over time (odds ratio [OR], 1.846; p < 0.001). Year-to-year trend analysis demonstrated significant increases in both the overall CT referral rate (OR, 1.192; p < 0.001) and the proportion of positive CT (OR, 1.335; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Our research suggests that AI may help cardiologists' interpretation of CXR by facilitating the identification of unexpected pulmonary abnormalities and enhancing proper clinical decision-making and further diagnostic evaluation with continued use.

title: Retroperitoneal Hybrid Nerve Sheath Tumor Mimicking Malignant Imaging Manifestations: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Hybrid peripheral nerve sheath tumors (hPNSTs) is an exceedingly rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor, featuring elements from at least two nerve sheath tumor cells. We herein report a rare case of retroperitoneal HNST manifesting malignant imaging features. Case presentation: We reported a 40-year-old female presented with unexplained abdominal pain, with no significant personal or familial medical history. Imaging workup revealed a large solid-cystic retroperitoneal mass with internal hemorrhage, calcification and cystic degeneration. The lesion showed restricted diffusion and progressive delayed enhancement on MRI, with blurred borders adjacent to major retroperitoneal vessels and the right ureter, highly suggestive of an invasive malignant tumor. The patient underwent complete surgical resection. Postoperative histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed a benign hybrid schwannoma/neurofibroma, with no lymph node metastasis identified. The patient recovered uneventfully and remained recurrence-free during follow-up. Conclusions: Retroperitoneal hPNST can exhibit atypical imaging features that closely resemble malignant neurogenic tumors. Accurate diagnosis relies on the combined analysis of radiological findings and immunohistochemical results. This case expands the known anatomical and imaging spectrum of hPNSTs, improves clinicians’ overall recognition of this rare disease.

Background: Hybrid peripheral nerve sheath tumors (hPNSTs) is an exceedingly rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor, featuring elements from at least two nerve sheath tumor cells. We herein report a rare case of retroperitoneal HNST manifesting malignant imaging features. Case presentation: We reported a 40-year-old female presented with unexplained abdominal pain, with no significant personal or familial medical history. Imaging workup revealed a large solid-cystic retroperitoneal mass with internal hemorrhage, calcification and cystic degeneration. The lesion showed restricted diffusion and progressive delayed enhancement on MRI, with blurred borders adjacent to major retroperitoneal vessels and the right ureter, highly suggestive of an invasive malignant tumor. The patient underwent complete surgical resection. Postoperative histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed a benign hybrid schwannoma/neurofibroma, with no lymph node metastasis identified. The patient recovered uneventfully and remained recurrence-free during follow-up.

Conclusions:

Retroperitoneal hPNST can exhibit atypical imaging features that closely resemble malignant neurogenic tumors. Accurate diagnosis relies on the combined analysis of radiological findings and immunohistochemical results. This case expands the known anatomical and imaging spectrum of hPNSTs, improves clinicians’ overall recognition of this rare disease.

title: Hepatic angiosarcoma misdiagnosed in a patient with occupational chemical exposure: A case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background: Primary hepatic angiosarcoma (PHA) is a rare but highly aggressive mesenchymal malignancy which is associated with occupational chemical exposures, particularly vinyl chloride, arsenic, and other industrial agents. Its preoperative diagnosis remains extremely challenging because its imaging features frequently overlap with those of benign hepatic hemangiomas, leading to potential misdiagnosis and catastrophic delays in management. Case presentation: A 65-year-old Han Chinese male with personal history of occupational exposure in a chemical plant for over 10 years presented to the emergency department with acute, persistent, severe right upper quadrant pain accompanied by nausea, pallor, and cold extremities. His blood pressure was 97/47 mmHg, and his heart rate was 103 beats/min. Three months prior, abdominal magnetic resonance imaging performed elsewhere reported a hepatic hemangioma (original records unobtainable). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a large hepatic mass with intratumoral hemorrhage and a satellite nodule in segment IV, suggestive of a ruptured malignant tumor. Given the patient’s stable hemodynamics, Adequate liver reserve, and resectable anatomy, emergency right hemihepatectomy was performed without perioperative complications. Postoperative immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of hepatic angiosarcoma, with positive staining for CD31, CD34, and FLI-1; negativity for AFP, CK7, CK19, and CEA; and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 10%, with P53 positivity. The patient initially recovered and was discharged, but telephone follow-up confirmed that he died approximately three months after surgery. Conclusions: This case underscores that in patients with a history of occupational chemical exposure, even remote exposure, a radiologic diagnosis of hepatic hemangioma should be interpreted with great caution. The rapid transition from misdiagnosis to spontaneous rupture and subsequent death within three months despite technically successful emergency resection, illustrates the fulminant clinical course of PHA. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion, consider timely contrast-enhanced imaging and surgical intervention, and thoroughly counsel patients regarding the extremely poor prognosis, even after apparently curative surgery.

title: Ultrasound guided Glossopharyngeal and Maxillary Nerve Blocks for Perioperative Pain Control in Adenotonsillectomy in Pediatrics: Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Background: Adeno-tonsillectomy surgery in pediatrics is associated with increased postoperative pain and discomfort, so combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal nerve ( UGGNB ) and ultrasound-guided maxillary nerve ( UGMNB ) in pediatric patients undergoing adenotonsillectomy surgeries to validate previous findings & to help decrease perioperative opioid consumption and respiratory complications Objective: Efficacy of combined bilateral glossopharyngeal nerve block and bilateral maxillary nerve block on perioperative management of tonsillectomy under general anesthesia provide excellent analgesic profile & significant differences in food intake postoperatively. Methods: 40 Patients was randomly allocated into two groups: Block Group: 20 patients received combined bilateral UGGNB and UGMNB. Conventional Group: 20 patients received IV paracetamol 15mg/kg. Intraoperative hemodynamics were recorded baseline and at 15 minutes intervals. Quality of analgesia was assessed using Wong-Baker FACES scale for children more than 3 years of age up to 8 years of age and VAS score for older children every 30 minutes for 1 hours after recovery from anesthesia in PACU and every 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 hours postoperative after transferring to the ward. For postoperative pain therapy, if pain scale scores are ≥ 4, first was IV ibuprofen 7.5mg/kg immediately postoperative. Results: -Pain was assessed by VAS or FACES scores, according to patient age, postoperative after 30 min, then at 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 hours, where group B patients had significantly lower pain scores at all-time points (p≤ 0.043) except after 24 h (p=0.355). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly longer in Group B than in Group C (10.9±1.9 h vs. 5.1±2.4 h, p=0.001). -Time to first rescue analgesia was significantly delayed in Group B (P = 0.001). -There was no statistically significant difference in pethidine consumption between the two groups within the first 4 hours or over 24 hours (P=0.171). -Group B patients needed significantly less Paracetamol (70% vs. 100%, p=0.020), yet, with comparable dose to Group C patients (7.1±5.5 vs. 7.8±2.3 ml, p=0.608). Conclusion: Combined bilateral ultrasound-guided glossopharyngeal and maxillary nerve blocks provide superior postoperative analgesia compared to conventional multimodal analgesia with intravenous paracetamol for tonsillectomy patients. The technique resulted in significantly lower pain scores, prolonged time to first rescue analgesia, reduced supplemental analgesic consumption, shorter PACU stay, and higher parent satisfaction, all with an excellent safety profile. Trial Registration: on clinicaltrials.gov, ( NCT07379866) at 24 November 2025.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Pathology Foundation Models and Transcriptomic Integration for Glioblastoma Survival Prediction
abstract: Abstract Background Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive glioma difficult to stratify prognostically. Whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs) and RNA-seq profiles capture complementary phenotypic and molecular characteristics, yet their individual and combined value for GBM-specific survival prediction remains insufficiently characterized. Despite the promise of recent pathology foundation models to provide richer and more transferable image representations, their added prognostic value in GBM, either alone or in combination with transcriptomic data, has not yet been established. To address these gaps, this study evaluated deep survival models based on WSIs, RNA-seq data, and their integration for overall survival prediction in the TCGA-GBM cohort. WSI representations were derived by means of a general-domain ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 as a baseline, and five recent histopathology-specific foundation-model configurations. To disentangle modality effects from differences in sample size, models were evaluated in both full and size-matched cohorts. Results Under size-matched conditions, multimodal integration consistently improved performance over WSI-only modelling across all six WSI encoders, despite the use of state-of-the-art pathology foundation models. Multimodal models achieved median C-indexes of 0.614–0.698, with a significant overall effect of modality. The CONCH-v1.5-based multimodal model achieved the highest median C-index of 0.698. RNA-seq provided the strongest prognostic signal, with held-out median C-indexes of 0.629 and 0.632 under full-budget and size-matched training, respectively. WSI-only models achieved median C-indexes of 0.543– 0.587 under full-budget training and 0.512–0.549 under size-matched training. In this limited-size cohort and frozen-weight setting, WSI encoder choice did not significantly affect full-budget unimodal performance, and pathology foundation models did not systematically outperform the ResNet50 baseline. Overall, results suggest a positive but unconfirmed trend towards additional prognostic value in GBM from integrating histopathological and transcriptomic features. Conclusions In this limited-size, frozen-encoder setting, integrating WSI and RNA-seq improved performance over WSI-only modelling across all encoders. The CONCH-v1.5-based multimodal model achieved the highest overall performance, while multimodal integration showed a positive but unconfirmed trend over RNA-seq alone. Pathology foundation models did not provide a consistent prognostic advantage over the ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 baseline. Larger independent cohorts are needed to confirm the incremental value of multimodal integration.

title: Time-dependent spinal cord pathology defines a one-month window for established experimental cervical spondylotic myelopathy models in rats
abstract: Abstract Objective: The temporal pathology of cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) remains insufficiently defined. This study systematically characterized temporal neurological, histological, and ultrastructural changes in a rat model of chronic cervical spinal cord compression to define a potential pathological window of disease progression. Methods: Thirty Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly allocated to a sham-operated control group (n = 6) and four cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) groups (n = 6 per time point). Chronic cervical spinal cord compression was induced by implanting a hydrophilic polyurethane polymer sheet into the C5–C6 epidural space. CSM rats were evaluated at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, and 2 months after compression. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed to confirm spinal cord compression and exclude intramedullary hemorrhage or edema. Neurological function was evaluated using the Basso–Beattie–Bresnahan (BBB) locomotor scale and somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings. Gray- and white-matter pathology was assessed using hematoxylin and eosin (HE) and Luxol fast blue (LFB) staining, respectively. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to characterize ultrastructural alterations in neurons, axons, myelin sheaths, mitochondria, and microvessels. Results: (1) MRI confirmed sustained dorsolateral cervical spinal cord compression without intramedullary edema or hemorrhage. BBB scores decreased markedly during the first week and stabilized at approximately 16–17 by 1 month, whereas SEP latency remained prolonged and amplitude remained reduced. (2) Histological analysis showed progressive anterior horn motor neuron loss and dorsal column myelin damage. At 1 month, motor neuron counts had decreased to 13.83 ± 0.70, the myelinated area to 86.21 ± 2.36%, and the vacuolated area had increased to 13.79 ± 2.36% (P ≤ 0.001). (3) TEM revealed progressive mitochondrial degeneration, axon–myelin disruption, and microvascular narrowing. At 1 month, mitochondrial cristae had decreased to 4.30 ± 0.16 per profile, and the microvascular lumen-to-cross-sectional area ratio had declined to 31.00 ± 1.42%. These abnormalities persisted or progressed at 2 months, demonstrating that the pathological phenotype was established by 1 month. Conclusion: Cervical cord injury progressed in a time-dependent manner, and 1 month of compression may represent a critical pathological window for the CSM model.

title: NeuroRAD-FM: A Distributionally Robust Foundation Model for Precision Neuro-Oncology
abstract: Abstract Foundation models for neuro-oncology have shown promise for non-invasive molecular characterization and prognostication, yet their clinical utility remains limited by cross-institutional distribution shift and poor performance on under-represented molecular alterations. We developed NeuroRAD-FM, combining self-supervised pretraining, Group-DRO, and a multi-backbone ensemble to learn site-invariant imaging representations. NeuroRAD-FM is pretrained on 7,414 multi-sequence brain MRI examinations aggregated from multiple institutions and evaluated on independent glioma cohorts from UCSF (n = 111), UPenn (n = 95), and an in-house cohort (n = 292). Downstream tasks included automated tumor segmentation, molecular biomarker prediction, and overall survival prediction. Compared with conventional foundation models, NeuroRAD-FM learned more site-invariant features, improved tumor segmentation across tumor types, significantly enhanced molecular marker prediction, and increased concordance indices across all institutions. These findings suggest that integrating Group-DRO with a multi-backbone foundation model enables robust, site-invariant representation learning and substantially improves molecular subtype and survival prediction across diverse neuro-oncology cohorts.

title: Quadruple hourglass-like constrictions of the radial nerve in neuralgic amyotrophy treated by focal resection and in-situ autograft reconstruction: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Hourglass-like constrictions are increasingly recognized as a structural manifestation of neuralgic amyotrophy. When several constrictions occur sequentially within a main nerve trunk, it remains uncertain whether the entire affected segment is irreversibly nonfunctional or whether the intervening nerve tissue retains a longitudinal scaffold capable of supporting regeneration. We report a rare case of quadruple hourglass-like constrictions of the main radial nerve that provides clinical evidence for preserved regenerative capacity within the intervening nerve segments. Case presentation: A previously healthy 36-year-old woman developed severe neuropathic pain followed by complete left wrist and finger drop. Preoperative electrophysiological examination demonstrated severe left radial neuropathy, active denervation, absent or markedly reduced voluntary motor unit recruitment in radial nerve-innervated muscles, absent distal radial compound muscle action potentials, and absent superficial radial sensory nerve action potential. High-resolution ultrasonography identified four sequential constrictions from the mid-upper arm radial nerve to the origin of its deep branch. Surgical exploration was performed at approximately 4 months after pain onset. Three severe proximal constrictive foci were selectively resected, whereas the intervening structurally continuous nerve segments were preserved and used as serial in-situ autologous interposition bridges. The mild distal constriction was treated with epineurial neurolysis. Follow-up showed progressive motor recovery. At approximately 3 months after surgery, electromyography showed nascent reinnervation in proximal radial nerve-innervated muscles. Late electrodiagnostic follow-up demonstrated re-emergent radial motor responses, and ultrasound showed continuity of the reconstructed nerve across the three coaptation sites. At approximately 14 months after surgery, the patient had regained near-normal wrist and finger extension, with active thumb extension exceeding 45 degrees. Conclusions: This case suggests that severe functional impairment in neuralgic amyotrophy with multiple hourglass-like constrictions may be maintained predominantly by discrete constrictive barriers causing focal mechanical interruption or conduction block, rather than by irreversible degeneration of the entire involved nerve segment. Even when the affected nerve has undergone axonal degeneration and has been diseased for several months, preserved regenerative bands within the intervening segments may allow them to function as native conduits for axonal regrowth after the focal barriers are removed.

title: Successful Management of Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis Complicating Rheumatoid Arthritis with Whole-lung Lavage and De-escalation of Anti-rheumatic Therapy: A Report of Two Cases
abstract: Abstract Background Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (APAP) is characterized by elevated levels of autoantibodies against granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), resulting in the accumulation of surfactant proteins within the alveoli. Immunosuppressive therapy is generally considered harmful in APAP, but the clinical impact of reducing immunosuppressive therapy on concomitant connective tissue disease remains unclear. Case presentation Case 1: A 69-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in clinical remission on methotrexate, iguratimod, and salazosulfapyridine developed exertional dyspnea. Chest High-resolution computed tomography showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with a crazy-paving appearance, and APAP was diagnosed based on bronchoalveolar lavage findings and elevated serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody levels. Whole-lung lavage (WLL) resulted in improvement, but APAP recurred one year later and required a second WLL. During APAP management, anti-rheumatic therapy was gradually tapered and discontinued, and she remained free of both APAP recurrence and RA flare for two years after the second WLL. Case 2: A 67-year-old man with RA treated with salazosulfapyridine was found to have bilateral diffuse bilateral ground-grass opacities on routine chest imaging and was subsequently diagnosed with APAP based on a positive serum anti-GM-CSF autoantibody testing. Because he was initially asymptomatic with preserved oxygenation, careful observation was chosen. After disease progression, WLL was performed, followed by gradual tapering of salazosulfapyridine. APAP relapsed three months later and improved after a second WLL, by which time salazosulfapyridine had been discontinued. He has remained free of respiratory symptoms and RA flare without medication for more than five years. Conclusion In selected patients with RA who develop APAP, tapering anti-rheumatic medication may allow APAP to be managed without loss of RA control. These cases suggest a possible immunomodulatory role of anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies and indicate that careful re-evaluation and adjustment of RA treatment after the onset of APAP may help achieve a more favorable balance between APAP control and RA disease activity.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Pentraxin-3 Compared With N-terminal-prohormone of B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (Nt-probnp) and Tumour Necrosis Factor-α (Tnf-α) in Dogs With Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease
abstract: Abstract Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) is a novel biomarker of interest in cardiovascular disease and injury. Despite this, there is limited literature on PTX3 as a veterinary biomarker. Another ubiquitous inflammatory marker, tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), has been studied extensively in dogs with DMVD, with mixed findings. The N-terminal-prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a routinely used biomarker of canine cardiac dysfunction. This study compared the diagnostic utility of PTX3 with TNF-α and NT-proBNP in dogs with DMVD. Serum NT-proBNP, PTX3, and TNF-α were measured in 50 client-owned dogs diagnosed and staged according to the ACVIM stages A-D. Echocardiographic variables, radiographic vertebral heart score (VHS) and vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and quality of life (QoL) scores were assessed. The Kruskal-Wallis test was used to compare PTX3, TNF-α, and NT-proBNP levels between different stages of DMVD, and the Jonckheere-Terpstra test assessed whether serum biomarker concentrations showed a significant ordered trend across progressively worsening DMVD across stages. Spearman’s correlation was used to assess the associations between biomarker levels, disease stage, QoL scores, SBP, radiographic, and echocardiographic parameters. Concentration of PTX3 and TNF-α did not differ significantly across DMVD stages, while only NT-proBNP showed significant variation between stages (p = 0.02). Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test revealed a significant ordered trend in serum NT-proBNP (p < 0.01), but not PTX3 and TNF-α across DMVD stages. NT-proBNP correlated significantly with DMVD stage, QoL score, VHS, VLAS, and echocardiographic variables including LVIDdn, LA:Ao (p < 0.01), and EF%, FS% (p = 0.02). NT-proBNP remains a reliable biomarker for diagnosis, disease monitoring, and prognosis assessment in canine DMVD. Future studies employing larger longitudinal cohorts will be essential to better elucidate the role of inflammatory markers in canine heart disease.

title: Alveolar Bone Mineral Density Correlates with Lumbar Spine Bone Mineral Density During Romosozumab Therapy: A Prospective Observational Study In Osteoporosis
abstract: Abstract Early osteoporosis detection remains challenging because of the limited accessibility of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), sparking interest in the use of routine dental radiographs to assess alveolar bone mineral density (al-BMD). This prospective observational study evaluated the longitudinal changes in al-BMD during osteoporosis therapy, its association with systemic BMD and its utility as a screening and monitoring tool in female patients. al-BMD was quantified using standardized intraoral radiographs with reference phantoms, while systemic BMD and bone turnover markers were concurrently monitored. At baseline, al-BMD was significantly lower in patients with untreated osteoporosis than in both young and elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated high diagnostic performance for al-BMD in identifying untreated osteoporosis, showing a positive correlation with the lumbar spine BMD but not with the femoral neck BMD and the total hip BMD. During sequential bone-anabolic therapy, al-BMD significantly increased over time, eventually reaching levels comparable to those of elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Also, al-BMD changes like those observed in systematic BMD. These findings suggest that al-BMD derived from dental radiographs is a clinically promising adjunct for osteoporosis screening and monitoring treatment-associated bone improvements.

title: Chemotherapy-Refractory Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Concurrent Long-Segment Intramedullary Spinal Metastases and Brain Metastases:Case Reports and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background Intramedullary spinal metastases (ISCM) are an extremely rare complication of systemic malignant tumors affecting the central nervous system, with a very poor prognosis,Among these, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is particularly rare as a primary tumor.To date, there have been only seven documented cases of ISCM associated with esophageal cancer,In all cases, involvement was limited to a single segment of the spinal cord.This article reports the first case of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) with long-segment intramedullary metastasis in the thoracic segment during chemotherapy, complicated by concurrent brain metastases. Case Presentation A 69-year-old male patient with advanced ESCC (cT4N1M1, with liver metastases),After receiving three cycles of albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with cisplatin chemotherapy,The patient presented with acute pain in the left shoulder and right lower limb, weakness in the right lower limb (Grade IV on the Medical Research Council muscle strength scale), and decreased sensation in the abdomen.Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spinal cord revealed extensive intramedullary lesions spanning long segments from T1 to T12,Accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,at the same time, edema of the cervical spinal cord is visible, but there is no enhancement.A concurrent cranial MRI revealed one new annular enhancing nodule in the left frontal lobe and one in the right cerebellum.Given the widespread involvement of the central nervous system and the family’s refusal of surgery and radiation therapy, the patient died 15 days after discharge. Conclusion Even in patients in whom systemic chemotherapy appears to be effective, ISCM can still occur, possibly due to tumor cells crossing the blood-spinal cord barrier via the hematogenous route.Gadolinium-enhanced MRI and annular enhancement are key to the diagnosis.This case highlights that when acute neurological symptoms occur during cancer treatment, the threshold for ordering neuroimaging should be lowered,this allows for early detection, thereby giving some patients the opportunity to undergo palliative radiation therapy or surgery.

title: CBCT-based evaluation of inferior turbinate morphometry and uncinate process anatomy in relation to maxillary sinus mucosal thickness
abstract: Abstract Objectives: To investigate the independent associations of inferior turbinate (IT) morphometrics and uncinate process (UP) anatomical variations with maxillary sinus mucosal thickness (MSMT) on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 200 sinus sides from 100 patients were evaluated. MSMT was measured and sides were classified as mucositis-positive (≥1 mm, n = 100) or mucositis-negative (<1 mm, n = 100). IT dimensions (height, width, anteroposterior [AP] length, and volume) and UP characteristics (orientation, pneumatization, and superior attachment type) were assessed using On-Demand and ITK-SNAP software. Cluster-robust linear regression was performed to account for within-subject bilateral dependency and adjust for potential confounders. Results: In the final adjusted multivariable model, IT height and IT AP dimension were the only variables independently associated with MSMT. Lower IT height was associated with greater MSMT ( P = 0.02), whereas greater IT AP length was positively associated with MSMT ( P = 0.006). In contrast, IT width ( P = 0.76), IT volume ( P = 0.28), UP orientation ( P = 0.51), UP pneumatization ( P = 0.77), and superior attachment type ( P = 0.45) were not significantly associated with MSMT. Conclusions: Dimension-specific IT parameters, particularly height and AP length, rather than overall IT volume or UP anatomical variation, were independently associated with maxillary sinus mucosal thickness. These findings suggest that localized turbinate geometry may be more relevant to mucosal thickening than generalized turbinate enlargement or uncinate process morphology. Clinical Significance :Understanding the anatomical variations of the inferior turbinate and uncinate process on CBCT scans helps clinicians identify potential anatomical predisposing factors for maxillary sinus mucosal thickening, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning for sinonasal and rhinogenic pathologies prior to dental implant placement or sinus lift surgeries.

title: Reversible Adrenal Hyperplasia Associated with Chronic Etomidate Use: A Case Report with 3-Year Radiological Follow-Up
abstract: Abstract Background: Etomidate, a commonly used intravenous anesthetic, is known to reversibly inhibit adrenal 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1). Illicit electronic cigarettes containing etomidate have emerged in some regions, and chronic inhalation has been associated with acquired adrenal hyperplasia. However, the long-term reversibility of etomidate-induced adrenal hyperplasia after drug cessation has not been documented in the literature. Case presentation: We report a 33-year-old male patient who presented with recurrent fatigue, after approximately 10 years of 4-5 times per week etomidate-containing e-cigarette use. Laboratory evaluation revealed hypokalemia (serum K⁺ 3.37 mmol/L), normal morning cortisol (9.66 μg/dL), elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) (322.00 pg/mL), and normal aldosterone-to-renin ratio. Computed tomography demonstrated bilateral adrenal thickening (9.3mm on the right, 9.5 mm on the left). Genetic testing excluded CYP11B1 and CYP21A2 mutations, supporting an acquired etiology. The patient was advised to discontinue etomidate use. At the 3-year follow-up, the patient remained abstinent. Repeat CT imaging showed largely resolution of adrenal hyperplasia, with adrenal thickness reduced to 3.9-4.3 mm bilaterally, and biochemical parameters returned to normal range. Conclusion: This case provides the first imaging evidence that etomidate-induced adrenal hyperplasia is reversible upon drug cessation, with largely radiological resolution documented at 3-year follow-up. The diagnosis of drug-induced adrenal hyperplasia can be established through a combination of exposure history, biochemical profile, and imaging findings, even in the absence of genetic testing. Early recognition is crucial to avoid unnecessary invasive investigations or genetic workup. A conservative "watch-and-wait" approach after drug withdrawal appears to be appropriate for similar cases.

title: ThyroGuard-Net: A Sensitivity-Optimised, Explainable Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework with Evidential Uncertainty for Thyroid Nodule Classification
abstract: Abstract Thyroid cancer is a common endocrine malignancy and the most common diagnostic technique for thyroid cancer is ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (FNA) cytology. Although many researchers have utilized machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), recent studies still rely on small single-centre datasets, poor generalisation across institutions, class imbalance, lack of explainability and – crucially – insufficient focus on sensitivity. This article highlights the typical issues that have plagued studies over the past decade and offers the recommendation of a publicly available, relatively multi-center dataset, TN3K that can help mitigate those issues. This paper proposes a hybrid EfficientNet–Swin Transformer architecture for robust and efficient training of concept-attention networks, trained with a sensitivity-weighted Focal-Tversky loss, an evidential uncertainty module for indeterminate-case triage and a concept-bottleneck explainability layer based on TI-RADS. It presents a complete mathematical formulation for all components (pre-processing, dual-branch feature extraction, cross-attention fusion, concept-bottleneck explainability, sensitivity-maximising loss design, and evidential uncertainty estimation). The model was trained on TN3K and tested without further fine tuning on the external DDTI dataset with 87.95%/91.46%/85.60% (accuracy/sensitivity/specificity) on the test set, with an evidential triage rate of 13.03–16.95%, showing the cross-institution generalisation narrowed and clinically, calibrated uncertainty over previous single-mechanism methods.

title: Oscillatory Modulation of Tumor Microenvironment pH Enhances Simulated Therapeutic Response in Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract This study presents the BioOnco System as a computational proof-of-concept framework combining histopathological image classification with a two-dimensional reaction-diffusion model of normalized proton-field dynamics. The classification component used the publicly available BACH breast histopathology dataset comprising 400 microscopy images from four diagnostic classes: benign, in situ, invasive, and normal. The final pipeline extracted 1,536-dimensional features with EfficientNet-B3, standardized the features, and applied multiclass logistic regression. On a held-out test set of 60 images (15 per class), the model achieved 85.0% accuracy, 0.852 macro-F1, and a macro one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.952. Independently, the reaction-diffusion module was evaluated on a 60 × 60 spatial grid under four predefined conditions: control, chemotherapy, oscillatory modulation, and combined therapy, with 30 independent replicates per condition. The final mean normalized proton concentration was 0.7423 ± 0.0002 for control, 0.4600 ± 0.0000 for chemotherapy, 0.8693 ± 0.0002 for oscillatory modulation, and 0.2676 ± 0.0000 for the combined condition. The combined condition differed significantly from chemotherapy alone (independent two-sample t-test, p < 0.0001). These findings demonstrate distinct computational responses produced by the specified model parameterizations but do not establish clinical efficacy, experimentally demonstrate therapeutic synergy, or provide patient-specific predictions. Experimental validation and parameter calibration are required.

title: Application of CT-Based Three-Dimensional Reconstruction to Guide Anatomical Resection for Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformations in Children
abstract: Abstract Purpose To describe CT-based patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction for lesion-oriented anatomical regional resection and compare the short-term outcomes of three surgical approaches for pediatric congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM). Methods We retrospectively reviewed 185 children treated between July 2023 and March 2025: segmentectomy (n=62), lobectomy (n=66), and anatomical regional resection (n=57). Noncontrast thin-slice CT data were reconstructed using Mimics to delineate the lesion, bronchi, pulmonary arteries, and pulmonary veins. Perioperative outcomes and postoperative complications were compared among the groups. Results Age and weight did not differ significantly among the groups. Operative times were 95±5.9, 80±3.7, and 92±5.7 min, while chest tube durations were 4±1.3, 2±1.1, and 2±1.4 days, respectively (both overall P<0.001). Pneumothorax, subcutaneous emphysema, pneumonia, and localized atelectasis did not differ significantly. Radiographic compensatory pulmonary hyperinflation occurred in 2, 10, and 1 children, respectively (overall P=0.009). Conclusion Patient-specific 3D reconstruction provided an anatomically explicit basis for lesion-oriented operative planning. Anatomical regional resection was feasible; however, the observed between-group differences require cautious interpretation because treatment allocation was nonrandomized. Prospective multicenter studies with adjusted analyses and standardized imaging follow-up are warranted.

title: Medial Epiphyseal–Epicondylar Alignment and Clinical Outcomes After Adding a Medial K-Wire to Lateral Two-Wire Fixation in Gartland II–III Pediatric Supracondylar Humerus Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Closed reduction and percutaneous pinning is standard treatment for displaced pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures, but the optimal pin configuration remains debated. We compared clinical and radiographic outcomes between lateral two-pin and medial-pin–augmented (crossed) fixation, focusing on the medial epicondylar epiphyseal angle (MEEA) as a comparative outcome rarely used for this purpose. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 202 children aged 2 to 12 years with Gartland type II to III supracondylar humeral fractures treated surgically between 2016 and 2021. Group 1 (117 children) received two divergent lateral wires plus one medial wire via mini-open incision; Group 2 (85 children) received two lateral wires only. The decision to add a medial wire reflected a mix of surgeon routine and intraoperative judgment of construct stability, not a fixed protocol. Outcomes were the Flynn rating, loss of carrying angle and elbow motion, and the Baumann, humeroulnar, medial epicondylar epiphyseal, and diaphysiometaphyseal angles, measured at final follow-up against the uninjured side. The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure controlled for multiple comparisons. Results Mean follow-up was 28.4 months; groups were comparable at baseline. Operative time was longer in Group 1 (40.7 versus 24.2 minutes; p < 0.001). Group 1 showed less loss of elbow motion (p = 0.008) and higher humeroulnar (p = 0.010) and medial epicondylar epiphyseal angles (p < 0.001) — the largest difference measured, remaining significant after correction; loss of carrying angle was also lower (p = 0.047) but not significant after correction. The Baumann angle and Flynn rating did not differ. No iatrogenic ulnar nerve injury occurred. Conclusions Medial-pin augmentation was associated with better-preserved alignment and motion at final follow-up. MEEA may detect medial-column alignment differences not captured by the Baumann angle, making it the more sensitive comparative measure here, without increased nerve injury. Because allocation was non-randomized, these findings describe an association rather than proof of superior fixation strength, and support selective rather than routine use of the added medial wire. Trial registration: Not applicable. This is a retrospective observational cohort study of a previously performed surgical treatment, not a prospectively registered clinical trial.

title: Diagnosis of Persistent Left Superior Venacava in Children with Conotruncal Defects using Multi-slice Computed Tomography
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) complicates surgical procedures in children with conotruncal defects (CTD). Although multi-slice computed tomography (MSCT) is widely applied in preoperative CTD diagnosis, its role in detecting PLSVC and analyzing CTD–PLSVC associations has received limited attention. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of MSCT for PLSVC in children with CTD, while examining its type, incidence, and distribution. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 264 children with surgically confirmed CTD who underwent 320-MSCT. Image quality and radiation dose were assessed, and age-related variations in CT dose parameters were analyzed. MSCT findings of PLSVC were compared with intraoperative results. Results All MSCT images were diagnostic (mean subjective score: 3.45 ± 0.5; Cohen’s κ = 0.80). The mean effective dose was 1.02 ± 0.24 mSv, with significant age-related differences in radiation parameters. MSCT showed complete concordance with surgical findings. PLSVC was detected in 32 children (12.1%), with the highest incidence in pulmonary atresia. The most frequent anatomical type was double superior vena cava without bridging vein. Conclusions Low-dose MSCT provides accurate, non-invasive visualization of PLSVC and its anatomical variants in children with CTD, supporting precise preoperative planning. Routine MSCT evaluation of CTD should include careful assessment for PLSVC, particularly in pulmonary atresia, where prevalence is highest.

title: Gut Check! Effectiveness of Emergency Room Investigations for Acute Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Purpose Ultrasound (US) is the most used imaging modality in children with suspected appendicitis, with high sensitivity and diagnostic accuracy. Our institution utilizes a standardized US findings reporting system evaluating for appendicitis, which may obviate the need for CT scan if findings are consistent with appendicitis. In this study, we aimed to characterize the efficacy of our protocol for emergency room appendicitis workup and identify any risk factors contributing to a missed diagnosis. We hypothesize that < 10% of patients who underwent appendectomy presented within the preceding 14 days with symptoms of abdominal pain and our current investigative framework failed to identify acute appendicitis. Methods We conducted a single institution retrospective review of all pediatric patients who underwent laparoscopic appendectomy from 2020 to 2022 to determine the rates of prior presentation to the emergency department with a negative workup for acute appendicitis in the 14 days prior to formal diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Demographics and clinical characteristics were collected. Differences between groups were compared by using the Fisher’s Exact Test or Chi-Square test for categorical variables. Results A total of 1902 patients met inclusion criteria with a median age of 11.4 years (IQR 8.3, 14.4). Most patients were male (N = 1,094, 58%), white (N = 1,244, 65%), English speaking (N = 1,695, 89%) Sixty-two patients (3.3%) were seen in the emergency department for abdominal pain within 14 days prior to appendicitis diagnosis, and an additional six patients (0.3%) were seen within the prior 30 days. These patients were younger with a median age of 7.4 years (N = 4, 12.5%) (p = < 0.001) and more likely to be non-English speaking (N = 17, 27%) (p = < 0.001). Thirteen (21%) patients had an ultrasound at initial presentation, and an additional three (5%) had a CT scan. Ultrasound findings included: Category 1 (N = 2), Category 2 (N = 5), indeterminate (N = 1), free fluid (N = 1), dilated appendix (N = 1). At the time of discharge on initial presentation, these patients were diagnosed with constipation (N = 7), abdominal pain (N = 22), gastroenteritis (N = 14), and other (N = 10). Surgery was consulted on 8% (N = 5) of these cases. Missed appendicitis patients had a higher rate of perforation (45.2% vs 27.7%, p < 0.001) and longer mean length of stay (56 hrs vs 9 hrs, p < 0.001). Conclusion Patients who presented with acute appendicitis after an initial missed diagnosis are more likely to have perforation and longer inpatient LOS. While a protocolized emergency room diagnostic workup for appendicitis is effective, barriers to effective communication with patients may contribute to missed diagnosis and should be considered in clinical decision making.

title: MDT-guided language-model reasoning for spinal infection diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Spinal infection is a destructive vertebral disorder in which delayed recognition can permit neurological injury, deformity and systemic disease. Before definitive sampling, clinicians must reconcile disease course, laboratory tests and imaging; among infected patients, distinguishing tuberculous from non-tuberculous disease creates further uncertainty. Large language models could organize this dispersed evidence, but whether structured evidence organization improves diagnostic decisions—and how clinicians respond to its advice—remains uncertain. We developed an MDT-guided workflow: complementary evidence synthesis for infection identification, and source-specific MDT review with conflict reconciliation for tuberculous-aetiology differentiation. In two retrospective centre-specific cohorts, three locally deployed open-weight models were compared with a matched minimal zero-shot baseline on the same patient record, model and clinical question. We then examined clinician decisions in a paired multi-reader, multi-case reader study using fixed MDT-guided AI advice. For infection identification, balanced accuracy increased in all six model-by-centre comparisons, with mean differences of 3.63 percentage points at Centre A and 1.48 percentage points at Centre B. This pattern did not extend to tuberculous-aetiology differentiation, which showed a sensitivity–specificity trade-off and mean balanced-accuracy differences of -5.48 and − 5.40 percentage points. In the reader study, five clinicians made 1,716 matched reader–case–decision assessments; accuracy was 92.1% with fixed AI advice and 89.1% without advice (difference, 3.03 percentage points; fixed-reader case-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 1.47 to 4.55), with 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions. Structured MDT-guided reasoning consistently improved broad infection recognition across models and centres, whereas its benefit did not extend to tuberculous-aetiology differentiation. In the reader study, fixed AI advice produced a net improvement in clinicians’ diagnostic accuracy. These findings highlight the task-specific value and limitations of structured language-model reasoning in clinical decision support.

title: A Hybrid Complex Quantum U-Net for Enhanced Medical Polyp Image Segmentation
abstract: Abstract In this work, a hybrid segmentation architecture is proposed that integrates real, complex, and quantum computation within a U-Net framework. The model combines a ResNet-50 encoder for initial feature extraction, a complex-valued bottleneck convolutional block to preserve phase and amplitude information, and a quantum variational layer with eight qubits to encode global statistics derived from complex activations. The proposed model is evaluated on a polyp segmentation task using the PolipSet, Kvasir-SEG, and CVC-ClinicDB datasets, with direct baseline comparisons against a pretrained U-Net and SegFormer reported on PolipSet. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid complex--quantum U-Net achieves the best PolipSet performance among the compared models, with mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 79.36\,\%, while also obtaining 78.29\,\% on Kvasir-SEG and 85.07\,\% on CVC-ClinicDB; the corresponding Dice coefficients are 88.38\,\%, 87.51\,\%, and 91.63\,\%, respectively. On PolipSet, these values outperform baselines such as Attention U-Net with ResNet-50 (IoU 75.93\,\%, Dice 82.94\,\%) and SegFormer (IoU 72.97\,\%, Dice 80.86\,\%). These findings highlight the potential of integrating complex-valued and quantum layers within deep learning pipelines for medical image analysis.

title: Evaluation of Bone Mineral Density in Type II Diabetic and Nondiabetic Individuals in a Mandibular Load-Bearing Region: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Aim To evaluate and compare the Bone mineral density (BMD) of the mandibular first molar area in patients with type II diabetes mellitus (T2DM) compared with nondiabetic subjects by using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and its possible use in pre-implant treatment planning. Materials and Methods A prospective cross-sectional pilot study was conducted in 32 subjects, including 16 with T2DM and 16 systemically healthy controls. CBCT scans were obtained using standardised imaging parameters. Assessment of bone density was done by measuring greyscale values (GVs) in three regions of interest within the mandibular first molar region. These include the crestal bone, 2mm apical to the crest and basal trabecular bone. The mean grey scale values for both groups were compared using appropriate statistical tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant. Glycaemic status will be assessed by measuring Glycated Haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Results The diabetic group demonstrated significantly lower mean BMD than the nondiabetic group across all assessed regions (p < 0.005). Age-wise distribution revealed a higher proportion of diabetic patients in the 55–65 years group (62.5%) than in the nondiabetic group (43.75%), indicating a significant association with advancing age (p < 0.005). Statistical analysis was conducted using descriptive and inferential statistics, particularly the chi-square test and Student’s unpaired t-test. The tools utilised in statistical analysis were SPSS 27.0 and GraphPad Prism 7.0. Significance level (p<0.05). Conclusion Type II diabetes mellitus is associated with reduced bone density in the mandibular first molar region, as assessed by grayscale values on cone-beam computed tomography. Site-specific evaluation of bone quality before implant placement may improve treatment planning and assist in recognising patients who require modified surgical protocols. Clinical Significance A comprehensive implant site assessment supports predictive treatment planning, enabling customised implant protocols that improve prosthetic stability. Ongoing monitoring of glycaemic impacts aids effective risk stratification and helps develop evidence-based guidelines.

title: Frame-Based Stereotactic Surgery for a Deep-Seated Brain Cavernoma: A Case Report and Technical Video
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral cavernomas are the second most common vascular malformation of the central nervous system. While microsurgical excision is standard for accessible symptomatic lesions, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is preferred for deep-seated or inaccessible cavernomas due to the higher complication risk of open resection, despite carrying its own risks of delayed hemorrhage and radiation-induced injury. Frame-based stereotactic surgical excision may combine the targeting precision of SRS with the immediate efficacy of surgical resection while avoiding radiation exposure. Case Presentation: A 25-year-old female presented with a history of headache, photophobia, blurred vision, and intermittent vomiting. Examination revealed left lateral gaze limitation and bilateral papilledema. MRI demonstrated a 15×20×24 mm intra-axial lesion in the left thalamic region extending to the left cerebral peduncle, causing obstructive hydrocephalus, initially favored as glioma. After endoscopic third ventriculostomy and an inconclusive endoscopic biopsy, stereotactic partial excision was performed using a novel 3D-printed stereotactic frame. Intraoperative findings and histopathology confirmed cavernoma rather than glioma. The procedure was uneventful, with no hemorrhage on postoperative imaging, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day two with an intact neurological examination. Conclusion Frame-based stereotactic surgical excision using this novel low-cost stereotactic system enabled safe, precise debulking of a deep-seated, rare thalamic-peduncular cavernoma, achieving diagnostic confirmation and symptomatic mass-effect reduction without complications. This approach may offer a viable alternative for deep, eloquently located cavernomas where open microsurgery carries excessive risk and SRS risks incomplete treatment and radiation side effects, warranting further evaluation in larger case series.

title: MRI Radiomics for Survival Stratification in Glioblastoma: Benchmarking Against Clinical Variables in a Retrospective Observational Study of the UPENN-GBM Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and exhibits substantial biological heterogeneity not fully captured by conventional clinical and molecular prognostic factors. MRI radiomics has emerged as a promising approach for deriving quantitative imaging biomarkers associated with patient outcomes. This study aimed to compare conventional clinical survival modeling with MRI radiomics-based machine learning for survival stratification in a public glioblastoma cohort. Methods This retrospective study included 230 patients with glioblastoma from the UPENN-GBM dataset. Clinical variables included age, sex, Karnofsky Performance Status, MGMT promoter status, and IDH1 mutation status. A total of 144 MRI radiomic features were extracted and reduced to 61 after preprocessing and feature selection. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was developed using clinical variables, while a Random Survival Forest (RSF) model was trained using radiomic features. Model performance was assessed using the concordance index (C-index), and survival stratification was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results The clinical Cox model demonstrated moderate prognostic performance (C-index 0.635). Increasing age was associated with worse survival, while IDH1 mutation and MGMT promoter positivity showed favorable survival trends. The radiomics RSF model achieved comparable prognostic discrimination (C-index 0.653) and stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated significant survival separation between risk groups (log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusions MRI radiomics-based machine learning enabled meaningful survival stratification in glioblastoma and provided complementary prognostic information alongside conventional clinical variables. Further external validation is required before clinical implementation. Trial registration Not applicable.

title: Attention-Based Deep learning Network for automatic detection of Microsatellite Instability in endoscopy images
abstract: Abstract Background Microsatellite instability (MSI) is a clinically relevant biomarker in colorectal cancer (CRC). In this study, we employed a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model to differentiate between MSI and microsatellite-stable (MSS) status using endoscopic images. Methods A pathology-proven dataset was constructed from 986 colonoscopy images of 176 patients with CRC. The images were partitioned into training, validation, and test sets. Attention-based ResNet-50 and MobileNet-V2 DCNN architectures were trained and evaluated for their discriminatory performance. The area under the curve (AUC) was used as the primary performance metric, supplemented by accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and precision. Results In the test cohort, the MobileNet-SE model achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.852–0.896), a precision of 0.830 (95% CI: 0.787–0.863), a sensitivity of 0.714 (95% CI: 0.670–0.754), a specificity of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.815–0.882), and an accuracy of 0.782 (95% CI: 0.754–0.808). Conclusions These findings underscore the clinical utility of endoscopic images in MSI screening and establish a benchmark for an optimal MSI prediction model.

title: Dynamic Changes in the Vertebral Artery–Subclavian Artery Bifurcation Angle During Cervical Positioning: A Prospective 3D TOF-MRA Study and Implications for Transradial Neurointervention
abstract: Abstract Background: The transradial approach (TRA) is increasingly used for posterior circulation neuroendovascular procedures; however, catheterization of the vertebral artery (VA) may be difficult in patients with an acute VA–subclavian artery (SCA) bifurcation angle. Although cervical positioning is often used to facilitate catheter navigation, its effect on the VA–SCA bifurcation angle has not been quantitatively investigated. This study aimed to evaluate the positional changes in the VA–SCA bifurcation angle using time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA). Methods: In this prospective single-center study, participants underwent time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography in five cervical positions: neutral, 45° right rotation, 45° left rotation, maximal flexion, and maximal extension. The VA–SCA bifurcation angle was measured on coronal multiplanar reconstruction images. Changes relative to the neutral position were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. Results: After exclusion of patients with VA occlusion or anatomical variants, a total of 81 right and 75 left VA were analyzed. Cervical flexion significantly decreased the VA–SCA bifurcation angle (right: −8.06°, P < 0.001; left: −3.95°, P = 0.005), whereas cervical extension significantly increased the angle (right: 6.18°, P < 0.001; left: 6.60°, P < 0.001). Cervical rotation produced no significant changes. Conclusions: Cervical flexion decreased, whereas cervical extension increased, the VA–SCA bifurcation angle bilaterally. These positional changes may influence VA accessibility during transradial neuroendovascular procedures. Cervical extension is a simple, cost-free, and readily applicable maneuver that may facilitate VA catheterization in selected patients.

title: Impact of Three-Dimensional Computed Tomography Reconstruction on Clinical Decision-Making in Revisional Bariatric Surgery
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Revisional bariatric surgery is increasingly common because of weight regain, insufficient weight loss, and postoperative anatomical complications, but conventional imaging often fails to provide comprehensive anatomical characterization. Three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography (CT)-based modeling may improve anatomical evaluation and surgical planning, but its impact on clinical decision-making remains insufficiently explored. Methods This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 40 consecutive patients referred for revisional bariatric evaluation between January 2021 and December 2024 at a tertiary referral center. All patients underwent standardized CT acquisition, 3D reconstruction, and gastric volumetric analysis, and were classified into a surgical group (n = 28) or a conservative management group (n = 12) after multidisciplinary assessment. The primary outcome was change in therapeutic management after 3D evaluation; secondary outcomes included weight-loss results, detection of anatomical abnormalities, gastric volumetry, and interobserver reproducibility. Results 3D modeling changed therapeutic decision-making in 42.5% of cases. Surgical plans were cancelled in 20.0% of patients, and 22.5% were reclassified for revisional surgery after 3D anatomical assessment. Anatomical abnormalities were identified in 75.0% of patients, including sleeve dilation (35.0%), intrathoracic gastric migration (15.0%), internal hernias (12.0%), and complex fistulas (8.0%). Gastric volumetry correlated strongly with weight-loss outcomes (r = 0.78, p < 0.001). Patients undergoing revisional surgery achieved significantly greater total weight loss than those managed conservatively (65.0% vs. 12.0%). Interobserver agreement for volumetric measurements was excellent (ICC = 0.96). Conclusion CT-based 3D modeling significantly influenced therapeutic decision-making in revisional bariatric surgery by improving anatomical characterization, identifying clinically relevant abnormalities, and supporting patient selection. These findings support 3D reconstruction as an adjunct in the multidisciplinary evaluation of revisional bariatric patients and warrant validation in prospective multicenter studies.

title: Texture-driven radiomics from longitudinal contrast-enhanced CT predicts short-term immunotherapy response in lung cancer: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Radiomic prediction of immunotherapy response has been widely reported, yet the nature and localization of the predictive signal remain unclear. We aimed to determine whether longitudinal delta-radiomics (change between serial scans) predicts short-term response in lung cancer, and to dissect the signal by benchmarking against pre-treatment and clinical models, separating texture from shape contributions, and localizing it across intratumoral and peritumoral compartments, and relating it to survival. Methods In a single-center cohort of 156 lung cancer patients receiving first-line immunotherapy, baseline and interim contrast-enhanced CT scans were analyzed. We extracted 1688 radiomic features from intratumoral, peritumoral (3/5/8/10-pixel shells), and combined ROIs, and computed delta features. Short-term response (RECIST 1.1) was modeled using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with all feature selection (univariate filtering, correlation pruning, LASSO) performed inside each training fold. Performance was evaluated by pooled out-of-fold AUC (mean over 5 seeds; 2000-sample bootstrap 95% CI). PFS and OS were assessed by C-index, Kaplan–Meier, and Cox models on cross-validation-averaged risk scores. Results Pre-treatment radiomics was uninformative across all ROIs (AUC 0.48–0.54), as were clinical variables (AUC 0.45). Intratumoral delta-radiomics predicted response with AUC 0.78 (95% CI 0.70–0.85). The signal was texture-driven: texture-only delta reproduced full performance (AUC 0.78), with five of six retained features being texture-based. The effect was consistent across all ROIs and peritumoral distances (AUC 0.74–0.78), and adding clinical, peritumoral, or multi-ROI features provided no improvement. The delta score modestly stratified PFS (HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.15–2.39; log-rank p = 0.006; C-index 0.56) but was not associated with OS (p = 0.28); prognostic signal resided specifically in intratumoral-containing ROIs. Conclusions The predictive information in serial CT is texture-driven, intratumoral, and exists only as change — it is not a restatement of tumor shrinkage, does not require peritumoral sampling, and is absent from static pre-treatment imaging. Longitudinal radiomics functions as an early response surrogate that partially tracks progression but does not predict overall survival.

title: Prediction of non-surgical spinal decompression efficacy in lumbar disc herniation patients is based on pre-treatment paravertebral muscle MRI radiomics and clinical factors in a two-center study with external validation.
abstract: Abstract Purpose To develop and validate a predictive model combining pretreatment axial lumbar MRI radiomic features of paravertebral muscles with clinical factors for assessing treatment response to the Non-surgical Spinal Decompression System (SDS) in patients with lumbar disc herniation (LDH). Methods This retrospective dual-center study included 766 LDH patients who underwent SDS. Radiomic features were extracted from segmented multifidus, erector spinae, and psoas major muscles on axial MRI. Six data modalities were constructed and compared using five machine-learning algorithms, with evaluation via five-fold cross-validation and an independent external cohort. Key features were selected by LASSO regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed by ROC curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHAP was applied to quantify feature contributions. Results LASSO selected 11 nonzero-coefficient predictors (4 clinical variables, 7 radiomic features). Random forest was the optimal algorithm. The combined clinical-radiomic model achieved internal and external validation AUCs of 0.879 ± 0.039 and 0.835 ± 0.038, significantly outperforming the clinical-only and all single-modality models ( P < 0.05). SHAP showed clinical variables accounted for 53.8% of predictive contribution, with age as the strongest feature. Calibration was good (Hosmer-Lemeshow P > 0.05), and decision curve analysis confirmed positive net benefit across a wide threshold range (0.05–0.85). Conclusion The combined clinical-radiomic model demonstrates good predictive performance for SDS outcomes in LDH patients and holds promise as a clinically useful decision-support tool.

title: Spondylodiscitis due to Stenotrophomonas maltophilia after endoscopic spine surgery: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background. Infection after endoscopic spine surgery is rare, but without timely diagnosis and treatment it can cause severe vertebral destruction. Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an intrinsically multidrug-resistant, non-fermenting gram-negative bacillus and an exceptionally rare cause of spinal infection. Case presentation. We report a 54-year-old immunocompetent woman who underwent interlaminar endoscopic discectomy for a right L4–L5 disc herniation. Mechanical low back pain began on postoperative day 3 without fever. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on day 52 demonstrated L4–L5 spondylodiscitis. A positive interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) led to a presumptive diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis treated with a 2RHZE/10RHE regimen, followed by empirical meropenem plus vancomycin; both failed. By day 87, imaging showed osteolysis of the inferior endplate of L4, and the Spinal Instability Spondylodiscitis Score (SISS) was 7, indicating potential instability. The patient underwent posterior L2–S1 instrumentation with L4–L5 debridement. Intraoperative cultures grew S. maltophilia , whereas tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and culture were negative. She received combination levofloxacin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) for six weeks. At 18 months she was pain-free with stable imaging, and the instrumentation was removed. Conclusions. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of S. maltophilia spondylodiscitis after endoscopic spine surgery. Early mechanical back pain after endoscopic discectomy - even without fever or leukocytosis - should raise suspicion for infection, and specimens for culture should be obtained before empirical antibiotic therapy is started.

title: Individualized Adjuvant Chemotherapy Guided by Pharmacogenomic Testing in a 14-Year-Old with Undifferentiated Embryonal Sarcoma of the Liver
abstract: Abstract Background Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver (UESL) is a rare, aggressive mesenchymal tumor in children, with historically poor prognosis. No standardized adjuvant chemotherapy exists. Pharmacogenomic testing can individualize treatment by predicting drug efficacy and toxicity based on genetic polymorphisms, but its application in UESL has not been reported. Case presentation We report a 14-year-old male presenting with right upper quadrant pain and fever. Imaging revealed a large mixed cystic-solid mass in the right hepatic lobe. He underwent R0 right hemihepatectomy. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed UESL with a Ki-67 index of 40%. Postoperative multigene pharmacogenomic testing (84-gene panel) identified key polymorphisms in TP53, ABCB1, and ERCC1, which guided selection of an individualized adjuvant chemotherapy regimen (VDC/IE: vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide, etoposide). The patient completed six cycles without dose reduction or delay, experiencing only grade 1–2 myelosuppression. At 36 months postoperatively, imaging showed no recurrence or metastasis, and the patient had returned to all normal activities. Conclusions This is the first report of systematic multigene pharmacogenomic testing to guide adjuvant chemotherapy in UESL. The patient achieved 36-month disease-free survival with favorable tolerability, a result comparable to or better than historical outcomes with empirical therapy. This case supports the integration of pharmacogenomic testing into individualized treatment strategies for rare sarcomas. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: Cone-Beam CT–Guided Thin Linear EBUS Bronchoscopic Biopsy of a Non- Peripheral Lung Nodule: Highlighting the Effect of Bronchoscopic Tools on CT-to-Body Divergence: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate bronchoscopic biopsy of non-peripheral pulmonary nodules adjacent to proximal segmental airways remains challenging. Such lesions lie beyond the reach of standard endobronchial ultrasound transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) and resist accurate bronchoscope angulation in proximal, less flexible bronchi. Case presentation: A 43-year-old non-smoking male was referred for biopsy of an incidentally found 16-mm solid right upper lobe nodule located adjacent to the second subsegmental branch (RB3b). The procedure was performed under general anaesthesia using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)–guided thin linear EBUS bronchoscopy (UCP190F, Olympus; 5.9-mm distal diameter). Intraprocedural CBCT acquisition enabled nodule segmentation and biopsy pathway planning overlaid on augmented fluoroscopy. Real-time ultrasound confirmed lesion localisation. During close-range bronchoscope manipulation, articulation of the bronchoscope tip caused reproducible displacement of the lesion relative to the augmented fluoroscopic target — a phenomenon we term bronchoscope- or tool-induced divergence, distinct from the established concept of CT-to-body divergence. Fine-needle aspiration under simultaneous ultrasound and augmented fluoroscopic guidance, with rapid on-site cytology, confirmed lesional material. Three cryobiopsies were then obtained using a 1.1-mm cryoprobe (Erbe, Tübingen) via the working channel in a wedged, stabilised position. The patient was discharged the same day; histopathology confirmed a typical carcinoid tumour. Conclusions: CBCT-guided bronchoscopy using a thin linear EBUS bronchoscope is feasible for non-peripheral lung nodules in anatomically challenging locations. Awareness of bronchoscope- and tool-induced divergence is clinically relevant and should be considered alongside CT-to-body divergence when targeting accuracy is suboptimal, particularly in proximal airways.

title: Prenatal Diagnosis and Genetic Etiology of Fetal Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Single-Center Retrospective Study of 147 Cases in Yunnan Province, Southwest China
abstract: Abstract Background Fetal polycystic kidney disease (FPDK) is a common ultrasound finding, but its genetic causes vary widely, and data from Yunnan Province are scarce. We aimed to fill this gap by systematically testing a large local cohort. Methods We reviewed 147 FPDK cases seen at our center in Yunnan between 2020 and 2024. All had karyotyping and CNV-seq as first-line tests. Families who tested negative on both were offered trio whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES). Outcomes came from medical records or phone calls. Results Karyotyping detected 18 chromosomal abnormalities (12.2%) mostly trisomy 21 (n = 10), trisomy 13 (n = 3), trisomy 18 (n = 1), 45,X (n = 1), and 47,XXY (n = 1) plus two structural rearrangements. CNV-seq identified isolated pathogenic CNVs in 14 cases (9.5%), ten of which (71.4%) were 17q12 deletions involving HNF1B. Among 32 families who went on to trio-WES, we identified diagnostic single gene variants in 19 (59.4% of those tested, 12.9% overall). The main culprits were PKD1 (n = 6), PKHD1 (n = 4), BBS2 (n = 2), and one each of BBS7 , TMEM67 , TMEM237 , NEK8 , VHL , HNF1B , HDAC8 , CELSR1 , BUB1B , and GRIN1 . All told, we found a genetic cause in 51 of 147 cases (34.7%). Of these, 44 families (86.3%) chose to terminate. Conclusions In this Yunnan cohort, trisomy 21, 17q12 deletion, and PKHD1 / PKD1 mutations were the leading causes. A two-step approach parallel karyotyping and CNV-seq first, then trio-WES for negatives greatly improves detection and gives families essential information for decision‑making. These results offer much needed regional data for prenatal counseling in Yunnan and surrounding areas.

title: Multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of recurrent glioblastoma - a multi-centre UK questionnaire study
abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent glioblastoma (GB) carries a poor prognosis, with physical and cognitive decline significantly affecting patients’ survival and quality of life. Unlike newly-diagnosed GB, there is a paucity of level 1 evidence to guide management, including uncertainty regarding the clinical efficacy and cost-effectiveness of repeat resection prior to second-line chemotherapy. We surveyed UK neuro-oncology specialists to evaluate decision-making practices regarding recurrent GB management and the clinical features influencing them. Methods Between December 2023 and April 2024, a 35-item questionnaire was distributed to consultant neuro-oncologists and neuro-oncology surgeons. Respondents were presented with seven case vignettes simulating first GB recurrences and asked to select suitable treatments, including their single preferred option. We also explored which factors routinely influenced decision-making and extent of multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement. Results Thirty-eight responses came from 23 consultant neuro-oncology surgeons and 15 consultant neuro-oncologists across 22 NHS hospitals (response rate 73%). Only 71% routinely re-discussed first recurrence at MDT meetings, with higher re-presentation rates among surgeons. Use of advanced imaging to confirm recurrence was variable: MRI perfusion (74%), MR spectroscopy (53%) and no routine advanced imaging (24%). Across seven vignettes, repeat resection followed by second-line chemotherapy was favoured in focally-restricted and late recurrences, but rarely considered for deep-seated or multifocal disease. Second-line chemotherapy was deemed feasible in most scenarios. Re-irradiation was rarely selected, except in late recurrence with good performance status. Best supportive care was often identified as feasible alongside active treatments, particularly with poor prognostic indicators. Factors most commonly influencing re-resection decisions included recurrence interval, performance status, anticipated extent of resection, eloquence and number of tumour foci. Conclusions Substantial inter-clinician variability in preferred management suggests a high degree of clinical equipoise. In this context, there is strong support for randomised trials exploring the clinical efficacy of different management options in recurrent GB, including re- resection surgery.

title: Active learning improves annotation efficiency for colposcopic lesion segmentation under a fixed labeling budget
abstract: Abstract Background: Pixel-level annotation is a major bottleneck in the development of colposcopic lesion segmentation models, particularly when expert annotation resources are limited. This study aimed to determine whether active learning could improve segmentation performance under a fixed annotation budget using a single-center clinical colposcopy dataset. Methods: We implemented a pool-based, batch-mode active learning framework with one warm-start stage and three acquisition rounds. All strategies started with the same 8 labeled images and acquired exactly 15 images per round, resulting in a final labeled pool of 53 images. Six acquisition strategies were compared under the same annotation budget: random sampling, predictive entropy sampling, entropy-MC sampling, K-means representative sampling, Borda-Image, and Borda-Batch. During the retrospective simulation, reference masks in the unlabeled pool were hidden and revealed only after the corresponding images were selected. Models were evaluated on the held-out test set using Dice, intersection-over-union, precision, recall, and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance. Results: K-means representative sampling achieved the highest Dice score with DeepLabV3+ at 0.5246. title: Noninvasive Prediction of HER2 Expression in Bladder Cancer Using a Machine Learning Model Based on Ultrasound Radiomics: Facilitating Precision Screening for ADC Targeted Therapy
abstract: Abstract Objective: To construct and validate an interpretable machine learning model based on ultrasound radiomics for the preoperative prediction of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) expression status in patients with bladder cancer. Methods: This retrospective study included 270 patients with pathologically confirmed bladder cancer, all of whom underwent conventional ultrasound examination preoperatively. Radiomic features were extracted from ultrasound images and subjected to feature selection using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation analysis, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Four machine learning algorithms, namely, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Random Forest (RF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), were employed to construct predictive models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. The SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method was applied for interpretability analysis of the optimal model. Results: A total of 1,288 radiomic features were extracted, of which 5 optimal features were retained for model construction after feature selection. In the test set, the XGBoost model achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.817 (95% CI: 0.634–0.999). Conclusion: The interpretable machine learning model based on ultrasound radiomics can preoperatively and noninvasively predict HER2 expression status in bladder cancer, providing valuable reference information for clinical decision-making in individualized ADC-targeted therapy strategies.
