title: Automated Brachial Plexus Localization in Ultrasound Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Accurate localization of the brachial plexus in ultrasound images is critical for regional anesthesia and perioperative care. Traditional manual interpretation is time-consuming and operator-dependent, while segmentation-based deep learning models, though precise, often demand substantial computational resources, limiting deployment in resource-constrained settings. This study evaluated lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for automated classification of brachial plexus nerve location into four anatomical quadrants, balancing predictive performance with computational efficiency for point-of-care (POC) environments. Methods: B-mode ultrasound images from the Kaggle Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation dataset were transformed from segmentation masks into a five-class classification task. Three CNN backbones—ResNet34, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0—were trained using 3-fold cross-validation. Data augmentation and class-balancing strategies were applied. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and pairwise statistical testing. Results All three models achieved comparable overall performance, with mean accuracies ranging from 0.7288 to 0.7320 and macro-averaged F1-scores from 0.7333 to 0.7365. ResNet34 had the highest mean accuracy and F1-score, though differences between architectures were not statistically significant. Per-class analysis revealed strong performance for majority classes (0 and 2) and lower precision and F1-scores for minority classes, particularly class 3. MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 demonstrated high computational efficiency suitable for on-device deployment. Conclusion Lightweight CNN backbones provide reliable performance for brachial plexus quadrant classification in ultrasound images. While ResNet34 offered marginally higher accuracy, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 provided better suitability for POC deployment due to lower computational requirements. Future work should address class imbalance and expand evaluation to larger, more diverse datasets.

title: A tunable Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus for patient-free retinal imaging validation
abstract: Abstract The validation of novel retinal imaging techniques and motion-correction algorithms is often constrained by biological variability and the lack of ground-truth data in \textit{in vivo} measurements. To address this limitation, patient-free validation platforms require standardized targets that mimic selected optical and structural properties of the human eye. Here, we present a Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus (SVEF), a perfusable and contrast-tunable microfluidic insert designed for ophthalmic eye phantom platforms. The SVEF features a high-density, retinal-like vascular network fabricated by soft lithography using a custom polydimethylsiloxane-zinc oxide (PDMS--ZnO) composite. This substrate acts as a bright, diffusely scattering background, while perfusion with hemoglobin solutions generates physiologically relevant absorbing vessel-like structures. By optimizing the hemoglobin concentration, we achieved a vessel-to-background contrast closely matching that of \textit{in vivo} human fundus images. We validated the SVEF as a robust structural reference for image registration, demonstrating accurate retrieval of imposed saccade-like micro-displacements and enabling the enhancement of multi-frame fluorescence imaging. Finally, we confirmed the compatibility of the device with biological assays by successfully integrating and imaging human iPSC-derived retinal neurons. The SVEF provides a reproducible, patient-free environment for benchmarking ophthalmoscopic systems, optimizing image-registration pipelines and supporting versatile \textit{in vitro} retinal experiments.

title: A Resource-Constrained Evaluation of Fine-Tuned Deep Learning and Local Zero-Shot Vision-Language Models for Brain MRI Slice Classification
abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned deep learning (DL) classifiers report near-saturated performance on public brain MRI slice datasets, but dataset leakage, lack of patient-level metadata, and limited robustness evaluation restrict their interpretation. Concurrently, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) enable zero-shot image understanding, yet their unadapted zero-shot performance under local hardware constraints remains unverified. We conducted a paired evaluation comparing fine-tuned DL architectures (ResNet18, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16) across three seeds against local zero-shot MLLMs (Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, MedGemma-4B) on a locked, leakage-screened 260-image four-class evaluation set using a single NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU (10 GB). We evaluated ImageNet pretraining on ResNet18, executed a 35,100-inference controlled corruption matrix across five synthetic transformations, and compiled a frozen 24-case Grad-CAM failure gallery. Fine-tuned ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved the highest mean Macro-F1 (0.9610 ± 0.0041), followed by EfficientNet-B0 (0.9531 ± 0.0069), pretrained ResNet18 (0.9476 ± 0.0024), and ViT-B/16 (0.9284 ± 0.0157). ImageNet pretraining exceeded scratch training by +0.0617 Macro-F1 (95% CI [0.0077, 0.1192]; scratch seed SD 0.0515), though scratch models exhibited marked seed-level initialization sensitivity. The strongest local zero-shot MLLM (Qwen3-VL-8B) reached Macro-F1 0.3991, yielding a large observed performance gap under the tested zero-shot, label-only setting (McNemar p < 0.001). Under corruptions, ConvNeXt-Tiny had the numerically lowest mean Macro-F1 drop (0.0253). Grad-CAM maps revealed spatial shifts during perturbation failures, though focal maps were also observed in misclassified cases. Under constrained local compute, which restricts deployable model parameter scale, the tested fine-tuned DL models substantially outperformed the unadapted zero-shot MLLMs evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning on this slice-level benchmark. High in-domain scores must be interpreted conservatively alongside dataset provenance, corruption sensitivity, and post-hoc explanation limits.

Under constrained local compute, which restricts deployable model parameter scale, the tested fine-tuned DL models substantially outperformed the unadapted zero-shot MLLMs evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning on this slice-level benchmark. High in-domain scores must be interpreted conservatively alongside dataset provenance, corruption sensitivity, and post-hoc explanation limits.

title: Relative contributions of reconstruction pipeline and MRI field strength to hippocampal shape variation
abstract: Abstract Objective Ultra-high-field 7T MRI provides increased signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution compared with 3T MRI, but contributions of field strength and reconstruction methodology to whole-hippocampus shape remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated their relative contributions to hippocampal shape variation. Materials and Methods MRI data were acquired from ten healthy adults scanned at 3T and 7T in a within-subject design. Right hippocampal 3D models were reconstructed using FSL, FreeSurfer, HippUnfold, and manual segmentation. Shape was quantified using geometric morphometrics based on 97 landmarks and semilandmarks. Procrustes ANOVA assessed effects of subject, reconstruction pipeline, and field strength. Results Subject was the principal source of hippocampal shape variation ( R² =0.194, P < 0.0001), followed by reconstruction pipeline ( R² =0.050, P = 0.0003) and field strength ( R² =0.025, P < 0.0001). Field strength and reconstruction pipeline interacted significantly ( R² =0.045, P = 0.0022). Hippocampal size showed significant agreement between field strengths ( r = 0.741, P < 0.0001), whereas shape correspondence was weaker but significant ( r = 0.371, P < 0.0001). FSL showed the smallest within-subject 3T–7T shape differences and closest agreement with manual segmentation. Discussion In this pilot cohort, reconstruction methodology had greater influence than field strength. Field-strength-related differences were modest relative to inter-individual and methodological effects, supporting whole-hippocampus morphometric analyses using 3T MRI under the evaluated imaging conditions.

title: The Role of Bronchoscopy in Acute Lung Atelectasis Due to Airway Mucus Plugging: A Case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Acute lung atelectasis caused by airway mucus plugging is a potentially reversible cause of respiratory failure, particularly in postoperative and critically ill patients. Prompt recognition and timely intervention are essential to prevent prolonged hypoxemia, mechanical ventilation, and other serious complications. Flexible bronchoscopy is considered the gold standard for diagnosing and treating obstructive atelectasis by directly identifying and removing airway obstruction. Case Presentation: A 32-year-old man developed severe hypoxemia and complete right lung atelectasis on the second day following exploratory laparotomy for abdominal trauma. Despite chest tube insertion, invasive mechanical ventilation, and supportive management, oxygenation remained critically impaired. Bedside lung ultrasonography demonstrated extensive right lung collapse. Therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy revealed complete obstruction of the right upper lobe bronchus by a thick mucus plug, with additional retained secretions in the right bronchial tree. Bronchial toilet and suctioning successfully restored airway patency. Immediate post-procedure chest radiography demonstrated significant right lung re-expansion, while arterial oxygenation improved markedly, with PaO₂ increasing from 40 mmHg to 194 mmHg. The patient was subsequently weaned from mechanical ventilation, experienced progressive clinical recovery, and was discharged from the intensive care unit in stable condition. Conclusion: This case highlights that mucus plug-induced atelectasis should be considered in postoperative patients presenting with sudden hypoxemia and radiographic evidence of lung collapse. Early therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment by restoring airway patency, promoting rapid lung re-expansion, improving oxygenation, facilitating ventilator weaning, and optimizing clinical outcomes when conservative management is unsuccessful.

title: Baseline Musculoskeletal Imaging Abnormalities and Subsequent Injury in Asymptomatic Athletes: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether abnormal baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or diagnostic ultrasound in athletes asymptomatic in the imaged region predicts subsequent same-region symptomatic injury. Methods A multi-database literature search was screened against prespecified criteria. Eligible studies imaged asymptomatic athletes before longitudinal clinical follow-up and reported an abnormal-imaging denominator. Risk of bias used the Quality In Prognosis Studies framework. Achilles and patellar tendon risk ratios (RRs) were pooled separately using exploratory DerSimonian–Laird random-effects models. Results Of 979 screened records, 78 reports were sought, 61 were assessed, and 16 reports representing 11 cohorts were included; four reports contributed six structure-specific estimates. In collegiate athletes, abnormal imaging predicted time-loss injury of the patellar tendon (adjusted RR 10.7, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.1–27.8), Achilles tendon (adjusted RR 19.2, 95% CI 6.6–55.7), and plantar fascia (adjusted RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.4–104.8). Pooled RRs were 5.43 (95% CI 1.28–23.13; I²=81.1%) for Achilles outcomes and 3.15 (95% CI 1.11–8.94; I²=83.4%) for patellar outcomes. Youth medial-elbow abnormality also predicted injury (17/59 vs 18/151; crude RR 2.42, 95% CI 1.36–4.31). MRI findings were less consistent. Conclusion Baseline imaging abnormalities identify higher-risk groups, most consistently on Achilles and patellar tendon ultrasound, but prediction is heterogeneous and many abnormal structures remain asymptomatic. Imaging should inform monitoring and contextual load management, not serve alone as an indication for restriction or invasive treatment.

title: Renal Vascular Complications Requiring Embolization After Partial Nephrectomy: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose To estimate transarterial embolization (TAE) incidence after partial nephrectomy and evaluate surgical-approach associations and treatment outcomes. Methods A sensitive literature search across PubMed, CINAHL, and Google Scholar yielded 506 records that underwent manual screening and extraction. Eligible cohorts required identifiable denominators and exact postoperative TAE counts; informative abstracts were eligible. Search dates and complete strategies were unavailable. Patient-denominator proportions and unadjusted within-study risk ratios were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung–Knapp intervals. Risk of bias used an adapted six-domain framework. Results Fifty-four reports were retained: 28 full texts and 26 abstract-only reports. The primary synthesis comprised 52 patient-denominator cohorts, 420 TAE patients, and 17,831 reported patient denominators. Pooled incidence was 2.70% (95% confidence interval 2.23–3.28%; I² = 64.0%); full-text-only incidence was 2.93% (2.19–3.92%). Two procedure-denominator reports were excluded from the primary pool. Robotic versus open, robotic versus laparoscopic, and laparoscopic versus open risk ratios were 0.55 (0.11–2.65), 0.34 (0.06–1.85), and 1.92 (0.84–4.40), respectively. Embolization frequently achieved reported hemostasis, sometimes after repeat treatment; renal functional findings varied. Conclusion Approximately 3% underwent TAE in reported cohorts, with substantial heterogeneity and no established surgical-approach superiority. Abstract-only evidence, surveillance differences, and possible cohort overlap limit certainty. Radiologists should distinguish imaging-detected lesions from treatment-requiring events and interpret embolization risk alongside clinical presentation and surveillance practices.

title: End-to-End Agentic AI Framework for Cross-Dataset Medical Image Classification Using CNNs, Vision Transformers, Explainable AI, Robustness Analysis, and LLM-Driven Clinical Reporting
abstract: Abstract Medical image classification requires more than high predictive accuracy. A practically useful artificial intelligence system must also provide reliable confidence estimates, robust-ness under image perturbations, interpretable predictions, and meaningful reporting for downstream decision support. This project presents an end-to-end comparative medical imaging framework that evaluates Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers across three heterogeneous medical imaging tasks: Chest X-Ray pneumonia classification, Brain MRI tumor detection, and dermoscopic Skin Cancer classification. The evaluated architectures include ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, DenseNet121, DeiT-Small, and Swin-Tiny. The framework integrates transfer learning, class-imbalance handling, model calibration, bootstrap confidence intervals, robustness evaluation, failure-case analysis, Grad-CAM explainability, ensemble learning , and extensive performance metrics. In addition, an LLM-driven reporting component is incorporated to generate structured model-comparison summaries, explainability interpretations, and decision-support reports. The LLM layer is constrained to provide research-oriented assistance rather than autonomous clinical diagnosis. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN architectures remain highly effective for structured radiographic images, while Vision Transformers provide strong performance and robustness for more contextually complex Brain MRI and dermoscopic imaging tasks.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Proton Spectroscopy in the Evaluation of Complex Ring-Enhancing Intracranial Lesions: A Four-Case Series from Pacific International Hospital, Papua New Guinea
abstract: Abstract Background: Ring-enhancing lesions (RELs) remain a persistent diagnostic challenge in neuroradiology, as neoplastic, infectious, and granulomatous processes frequently overlap in their conventional MRI appearance. Accurate differentiation is critical for guiding management, particularly in resource-limited settings such as Papua New Guinea (PNG), where access to advanced neuroimaging is concentrated in a few centers and specialist manpower is limited. Study setting and design: This retrospective case series was conducted at Pacific International Hospital (PIH), Port Moresby, PNG, over four months (June–September 2026). Four brain MRI cases were included: three presenting as ring-enhancing masses, and one miscellaneous nerve sheath tumour at the craniocervical junction and C1–C2 level. Materials and methods: Of the four cases, two were referred from Port Moresby General Hospital and two were managed in-house at PIH. Conventional MRI sequences, supplemented by single-voxel MR spectroscopy (MRS) in selected cases, were used to evaluate metabolite profiles and to help differentiate primary brain tumour, metastatic disease, and infective processes such as tuberculoma. Results: One case, an 18-year-old male, demonstrated a cortical high-grade glioma with elevated choline-to-N-acetylaspartate (Cho/NAA >1.5) and choline-to-creatine (Cho/Cr >2) ratios, favouring a glial neoplasm despite an atypical age. A second case, a 29-year-old male with constitutional symptoms, showed multifocal ring-enhancing lesions with a preserved NAA peak and Cho/NAA <1, consistent with CNS tuberculoma and correlating with the clinical history. A third case demonstrated periventricular, splenial, and parieto-occipital rim-enhancing and serpentine lesions, radiologically indistinguishable between tuberculoma and neurosarcoidosis; tuberculoma was favoured on supporting clinical evidence. A fourth, miscellaneous case demonstrated a craniocervical/C1–C2 nerve sheath tumour with a characteristic dumbbell configuration on T2-FLAIR and post-contrast T1-weighted imaging. Conclusion: This first PNG-based series demonstrates the added diagnostic value of MRS in characterising ring-enhancing lesions and illustrates how strengthened referral pathways from provincial and district-level facilities to centres equipped with advanced imaging can accelerate diagnosis and improve management outcomes.

title: Probabilistic three-dimensional mineralogical characterisation of drill core using μXRF and XCT: application to the Nautanen North IOCG deposit
abstract: Abstract Accurate mineralogical characterisation of drill cores is important for quantifying variability and supporting geometallurgical interpretations. Conventional assays provide bulk elemental concentrations but do not preserve mineral distributions, whereas individual non-destructive methods provide only partial mineralogical information. In this study, a probabilistic integrated framework was developed for three-dimensional mineralogical mapping, using four drill-core samples from Nautanen North, northern Sweden, as a case study. Micro-X-ray fluorescence (µXRF) maps classified with the Advanced Mineral Identification and Characterization System (AMICS) were co-registered with corresponding X-ray computed tomography (XCT) surfaces to derive mineralogical labels, which were used as two-dimensional supervision for a deep learning segmentation model, with XCT responses as the input. Detailed mineralogy was consolidated into four XCT-supported classes: Matrix silicates, Quartz, Garnet and Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides. Generalisation was evaluated using nested leave-one-sample-out validation, and predicted class probabilities were calibrated to better reflect prediction reliability. The selected support-aware calibrated ensemble achieved a mean accuracy of 0.899 and a mean macro Dice coefficient of 0.583. Matrix silicates transferred most consistently, whereas the Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides class remained difficult to discriminate because of its heterogeneous and overlapping XCT responses. The calibrated ensemble was subsequently applied to predict the mineralogical classes within a half-core XCT volume. Predictions remained spatially coherent across the evaluated XCT volume, with high confidence, low normalised predictive entropy and high spatial agreement. The framework demonstrates the potential to extend targeted surface mineralogical observations into three-dimensional predictions of mineralogical classes, accompanied by class probabilities and uncertainty fields, that can support geometallurgical domain definition and the selection of suitable samples for additional mineralogical analysis or metallurgical testing.

title: Evaluation Metrics for Image Classification, Segmentation and Localization
abstract: Abstract Evaluation metrics dictate the incentives for an image analysis system, detect remaining failures, and verify any proposed improvement in scientific or clinical claims. Despite the mathematical similarity of classification, segmentation, and localization, the units, matching criteria, and practice implications vary across these tasks. The current review analyzes the distinctions through the lens of a selected sample of 150 bibliographically validated references, including 10 papers from the provided author profile. It incorporates foundational statistics, state-of-the-art benchmarking practices, medical imaging use cases, and recent developments in uncertainties, selective prediction, and deployment. The review organizes 72 metrics and corresponding evaluation quantities by the question they answer: correctness of decision, score discrimination, reliability of probabilities, spatial correspondence, recovery of objects, localization of geometry, or practical utility. Comparisons describe equations, assumptions, aggregation approaches, advantages, and failures. Ten deterministic worked examples demonstrate prevalence effects, constant discrimination and worsening probability scores, reverse rankings because of aggregation, hidden border failures by overlap, detection matching, physical landmark errors, and the cost of abstaining. Twenty-four numeric instances from 4 separate publications supply additional citations and examples without pooling the inconsistent results. The primary takeaway is that a sound evaluation requires a small and preselected set of metrics, complementary to each other, applicable to the defined population, unit, reference standard, and decision. For classification, operating point performance is always required, along with discrimination and probability metrics. Segmentation demands appropriate measures of overlap, borders, and object topology. Localization needs explicitly stated criteria of correspondence and tolerance and false positive control. Independent partitioning, uncertainties, subgroups, and workflow outputs determine the interpretability of the metrics. This manuscript is an organized critical review and methodology resource, but not a completed systematic review according to PRISMA criteria, meta-analysis, or benchmark of a new model. The attached list of metrics, reference export, extraction notes, computational code, and reporting checklist help design and validate reproducible studies and author reviews.

title: Brain Tumor Segmentation in the Foundation-Model
abstract: Abstract Automated brain tumor segmentation has progressed from handcrafted pipelines and U-Net variants to self-configuring 3D CNNs, transformer hybrids, state-space models, diffusion based segmenters, promptable models and brain-specific foundation models. Yet the field’s central scientific problem has changed: another fractional gain in Dice on a familiar BraTS split provides limited evidence that a system will remain reliable when MRI sequences are missing, scanners and institutions change, lesions are small or multifocal, postoperative anatomy is distorted, or uncertainty is high. This structured critical review synthesizes 150 references with emphasis on 2025–2026 and compares architectures, multimodal fusion strategies, preprocessing, missing-modality learning, self-supervision, foundation-model adaptation, federated learning, domain adaptation, uncertainty quantification and clinical translation. We organize evidence around adult glioma, pediatric tumors, brain metastases, meningioma and longitudinal/postoperative applications; distinguish region overlap from lesion detection and volumetric clinical endpoints; and critically examine leakage, site confounding, hidden test reuse, pretraining contamination, annotation uncertainty and challenge-overfitting. Recent evidence is especially informative: brain MRI foundation models such as BrainIAC and BrainFound improve label efficiency and cross-task transfer, while task specific systems such as nnU-Net and carefully engineered 2.5D/3D networks remain formidable full-data baselines. Missing-modality studies increasingly favor adaptive fusion, distillation and modality dropout over naive zero-filling; uncertainty work is moving toward conformal and evidential approaches that can identify cases requiring expert review; and external studies of metastases and meningiomas demonstrate why lesion-wise, site-stratified and human-in-the-loop evaluation is essential. We propose DATA-SEG, Dataset, Annotation, Train/test integrity, Architecture, Statistics, External robustness and Governance, as a reporting and evaluation framework. The review concludes that the next high-impact phase of brain tumor segmentation should prioritize post-cutoff hidden benchmarks, cross-site robustness, missing-sequence stress tests, calibrated selective segmentation, multi-rater probabilistic ground truth and longitudinal clinical readouts rather than leaderboard optimization alone.

title: Comparison of clinical and pathological characteristics between localized giant cell and fibroadenoma of tendon sheath
abstract: Abstract Objective: To explore the clinical and pathological characteristics of localized giant cell tumor of tendon sheath (L-GCTS) and fibroma of tendon sheath (FTS), and to compare and analyze them. Methods: 241 cases of L-GCTS and 41 cases of FTS who underwent surgical resection and diagnosis at Wuxi Ninth People's Hospital from 2019 to 2023 were collected. Clinical and pathological data of all cases were organized for retrospective analysis. Chi-square test was used to analyze differences between groups. Results: Comparing our two groups of cases, we found that L-GCTS is more common, while FTS is less common. However, the two were very similar in clinical features, disease course, age of onset, tumor size and overall appearance, as well as imaging manifestations; In our case, L-GCTS was more common in female patients, and there was no significant gender difference in FTS; L-GCTS was more common in the right hand, FTS was also more common in the hand, but the left incidence rate is slightly higher than the right, with no significant difference; In addition, a small number of L-GCTS were accompanied by damage to surrounding tissues, and 41 cases of FTS did not cause damage to surrounding tissues; L-GCTS and FTS are mostly single lesions, with a few being multiple lesions; Among 241 cases of L-GCTS, 235 were primary cases, 6 were recurrent cases, and 41 cases of FTS were all primary cases; The coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of L-GCTS was 89%, and the coincidence rate between preoperative imaging diagnosis and postoperative pathological diagnosis of FTS was 55.3%. The main reason was that it is easier to misdiagnose FTS as L-GCTS before surgery; There were certain differences in pathological and immunohistochemical manifestations between the two. Conclusion: L-GCTS and FTS are very similar in clinical features, disease course, predilection site, predilection age, tumor size, and tumor appearance. Imaging examination methods are difficult to distinguish between the two before surgery. The differentiation between the two mainly relies on histopathology and immunohistochemistry, and the two also exhibit different molecular genetics. Although both L-GCTS and FTS are benign tumors, their recurrence rates and other prognostic factors are different. Therefore, it is necessary to clearly distinguish between the two.

title: SOA-UNet: Sparse Otsu-guided Attention U-Net with Adaptive Boundary Loss for Lightweight Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of brain tumors from MRI images is fundamental but computationally intensive due to the tumor region's irregular morphology and heterogeneous intensity. This study presents the SOA-UNet architecture: a lightweight, high-accuracy deep learning model that incorporates sparse feature encoding with Otsu-based attention guidance along with an Adaptive Boundary Loss to achieve accurate localization of tumors with reduced computation. The proposed model utilizes Otsu's thresholding for prior attention, driving the network towards the most critical tumor regions; meanwhile, the sparse encoder removes redundancy and enhances feature discrimination. The newly proposed Adaptive Boundary Loss improves contour delineation while preserving structural integrity along complex tumor boundaries. This study proposes lighweight deep learning model with proper preprocessing that the model can work quickly in terms of training and testing with the dataset. The results position SOA-UNet as the most effective and deployable lightweight framework for reliable brain tumor segmentation, unifying interpretability, accuracy, and speed.

title: Super-Resolution and Artificial Transformer with Attention for accurate detection of brain tumor in MRI-based medical imaging
abstract: Abstract Medical image processing is a vital and rapidly growing field in healthcare and plays a crucial role in diagnosing severe conditions, such as brain tumors. Since brain tumors can be life-threatening, accurate detection through medical imaging is essential. Our research focuses on the accurate detection of brain tumors using deep learning techniques. In most cases, images are highly denoised, irregularly shaped, and either too bright or too dark, which makes accurate detection difficult. So our proposed work enhances significant features in brain images through a super-resolution technique, which improves diagnosis, detection, and up- scales the MRI images. We proposed a novel approach that combines an attention mechanism with an artificial Transformer model. Our model uses channel attention blocks separately to identify the complex features of the image in a channel, and pixel attention enhances the spatial information using a lightweight convolutional layer. This study used a publicly available magnetic resonance imaging dataset containing 7023 images. This work aims to improve the accuracy of tumor detection while maintaining robustness and computational efficiency in real-world scenarios. In addition, we compared our proposed approach with several state-of- the-art deep learning models, including MobileNetV3, DenseNet 121, ResNet 152, VGG 16, and other literature review results for comparative analysis. Our proposed lightweight model significantly enhances diagnostic speed and achieves an impressive precision of 99.16%, outperforming existing techniques.

title: Spectral CT reconstruction algorithm combining total variation and low-rank regularizations based on the Chambolle-Pock method
abstract: Abstract Spectral computed tomography (CT) utilizes photon-counting detectors to acquire multi-energy data for reconstruct images. Due to the limited number of photons in each energy bin, spectral CT imaging suffers from severe quantum noise, making clinical diagnosis more challenging. To address this limitation, we proposed a spectral CT reconstruction model combining total variation (TV) and low-rank regularizations. In the proposed model, the TV regularization was applied to suppress staircase artifacts in spatial domain, while the low-rank regularization was utilized to reduce noise by exploiting the correlation among the spectral CT images in the spectral dimension. To improve the efficiency of the spectral CT reconstruction algorithm, the Chambolle-Pock method was employed to solve our proposed model. Firstly, we constructed the spectral CT reconstruction model combining TV and low-rank regularizations. Secondly, within the Chambolle-Pock optimization framework, the dual variables were introduced to reformulate the reconstruction model as a convex-concave saddle-point problem, which was then transformed into a different equivalent form. Finally, we derived the closed-form solution for each sub-problem in this different equivalent form, thereby obtaining a single-loop iterative reconstruction algorithm. To validate the algorithm’s efficacy, simulated head and thorax phantom data experiments were performed. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the proposed algorithm’s outstanding performance in noise suppression, artifact reduction and detail preservation compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: Longitudinal Multi-Modality MRI–Ultrasound Cyst-Level Analysis of Polycystic Kidney Disease in a Feline Model: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Abstract Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) in Persian cats is commonly monitored using total kidney volume (TKV); however, this kidney-level metric does not capture heterogeneity in individual cyst dynamics. Here, a standardized longitudinal imaging framework integrating volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with serial ultrasound (US) is presented, enabling cyst-level analysis in a feline PKD model followed over two years. MRI-based volumetry quantified individual cyst growth rates and identified structural coalescence events, defined as the persistent loss of visible boundaries between adjacent cysts without implying luminal communication. Serial US provided high-frequency temporal context and supported MRI-defined trends, rather than replacing MRI-based structural assessment. The analysis revealed marked asymmetric progression, with significant enlargement and coalescence of right-sided cysts, while left-sided cysts remained stable. This dual-modality approach demonstrates the feasibility of integrating volumetric MRI with serial ultrasound for longitudinal cyst-level analysis, enabling the identification of asymmetric progression and cyst-level structural remodeling that may be overlooked by kidney-level volumetrics alone. Although based on a single case, this study demonstrates the feasibility of a standardized MRI–ultrasound workflow and provides a methodological framework for future validation in larger cohorts.

title: HLNet: High-Confidence Lightweight Network for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Semi-Supervised Learning(SSL) can effectively alleviate the reliance on large amounts of pixel-level labeled data when training fully supervised medical image segmentation models. However, most current semi-supervised learning approaches rely on self-training or consistency regularization methods, which are highly susceptible to erroneous supervision from low-quality pseudo-labels, thus affecting model segmentation performance. Additionally, existing semi-supervised backbone networks typically have large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for portable device designs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight semi-supervised segmentation model with high confidence under dual-level perturbations. Perturbations are applied at both the input data and model levels to guide the model in learning more robust feature representations. Furthermore, low-quality pixels are ignored, and EVidence Inference Learning(EVIL) is introduced to estimate the uncertainty of pseudo-labels, mitigating the erroneous supervision from pseudo-labels during training. Experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms comparison models on three different public datasets—ACDC, BUSI, and Promise12. With only 20% labeled data, the model achieves promising segmentation performance in terms of Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Jaccard index, while significantly reducing the number of parameters.

title: Extension of the phenotypic spectrum of BMP1-related disorders through a novel homozygous variant identified in a foetus with intrauterine growth retardation
abstract: Abstract Background Osteogenesis imperfecta encompasses a heterogeneous group of heritable connective tissue disorders characterised by bone fragility and skeletal deformities. Autosomal recessive forms of OI may result from defects in the BMP1 gene, which encodes two main metalloproteinases, BMP1 and its longer isoform mTLD, both essential for type I procollagen processing. To date, BMP1 -related OI has only been reported postnatally. Results We report a complex homozygous BMP1 variant identified by prenatal whole-exome sequencing in a foetus presenting a polymalformative phenotype at gestational week 23 + 2.Ultrasound findings included severe intrauterine growth restriction, bilateral clubfeet, cranial bone anomalies, and signs of cerebral hypoplasia. At this developmental stage, histological examination did not show features of osteoporotic bone structure. A combination of molecular and biochemical strategies led us to characterise the variant and the consequences on BMP1 protein expression as its biological activity in the processing of several substrates. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that the c.835A > G variant, located within the protease domain of BMP1, leads to (1) a deleterious missense substitution (p.Arg279Gly) affecting protease activity toward multiple BMP1 substrates, including procollagen I, thrombospondin-1, and chordin and (2) aberrant splicing, inducing exon 6 skipping, and a subsequent frameshift of the open reading frame. Conclusion This case broadens the phenotypic spectrum of BMP1 -related disorders and suggests a role for BMP1 in early human development beyond skeletal fragility. The findings support the inclusion of BMP1 in prenatal diagnosis gene panels for severe syndromic foetal presentations and underscore the importance of functional validation in variant interpretation.

title: Pitfalls of enzyme- based diagnosis of lysosomal storage diseases in children
abstract: Abstract Background: Fabry disease is uniquely inherited in an X-linked manner, in contrast to the autosomal recessive inheritance observed in Pompe, Gaucher, Niemann–Pick diseases, and Mucopolysaccharidoses (except Hunter disease). Each disorder is characterized by deficiency of a specific lysosomal enzyme, leading to accumulation of distinct substrates and subsequent organ-specific pathology. Purpose: This study aimed to assess the concordance between clinical findings, enzymatic, substrate and genetic testing in patients suspected of having rare lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs), with emphasis on cases showing diagnostic discordance, where enzyme assay and clinical evidence supports a disease despite negative ꜠substrate accumulation and genetic ꜠ results. Patients and Methods: The study included 46 cases from El-beheira governorate. Enzyme assay, substrate and genetic analysis were performed using the ARCHIMED life International Medical Laboratory platform, which offers testing for rare diseases with unlimited reanalysis incorporating newly discovered conditions until a diagnosis is achieved. Next generation Sequencing (NGS) was used for gene sequencing, while enzyme levels and their corresponding substrates were measured using tandem mass spectrometry from dried blood spots. Clinical evaluation of affected organs was conducted at the Damanhur Teaching Hospital by using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Results: Analysis of the selected LSDs demonstrated marked genetic and enzymatic heterogeneity despite shared lysosomal dysfunction. Hunter disease (MPS type 2) is uniquely inherited in an X-linked recessive manner. In contrast, Pompe disease, Gaucher disease, Niemann–Pick disease, and the rest of types of Mucopolysaccharidoses followed an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. Each disorder was associated with deficiency of a specific lysosomal enzyme, leading to accumulation of distinct substrates, including glycogen in Pompe disease, glucocerebroside (glucosylsphingosine) in Gaucher disease, sphingomyelins in NPD and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in MPS. Conclusion: This study identified patients with reduced enzyme activity and supportive clinical features despite negative genetic findings and normal substrate levels. These results highlight the limitations of relying solely on enzyme testing and emphasize the importance of integrated clinical, enzymatic, substrate accumulation and molecular assessment for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma involving an intraparotid lymph node: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma (formerly known as nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma) is a distinct B-cell neoplasm characterized by large neoplastic cells with multilobulated “popcorn-like” nuclei. It typically presents as peripheral lymphadenopathy and rarely involves the intraparotid lymph nodes, which may pose a diagnostic challenge due to overlap with other lymphoid neoplasms, particularly classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Case presentation: A 23-year-old man presented with a painless left parotid swelling. Ultrasound revealed a solitary intraparotid lymph node, and an excisional biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL). After the PET/CT scan, it was classified as Stage IA. He was treated with localized radiotherapy and remained clinically stable at 3-months follow up. Conclusion Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) rarely involves the parotid lymph nodes, presenting diagnostic challenges due to its indolent course and potential histologic mimicry of benign lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires excisional biopsy and immunohistochemistry, and treatment is stage-dependent. Despite a favorable prognosis, careful follow-up is essential because of the risk of relapse or transformation into aggressive B-cell lymphoma.

title: Pyogenic Liver Abscess Secondary to Acute Appendicitis: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Pyogenic liver abscess is uncommon in children, and acute appendicitis as an underlying cause is now exceedingly rare, having been replaced by hepatobiliary diseases as the leading etiology. When appendicitis does lead to hepatic abscess formation, the diagnosis is often delayed because children may present with nonspecific symptoms that mimic other common paediatric illnesses. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by an 11-year-old boy whose appendicitis-related liver abscess initially presented with fever and altered consciousness, leading to a mistaken suspicion of meningitis. The report emphasizes the need to maintain a high index of suspicion for abdominal pathology in febrile children with unexplained neurological symptoms and underscores the continued relevance of portal pyemia from a concealed appendiceal focus. Case Presentation An 11-year-old Iranian male presented with a three-day history of fever, altered mental status, nausea, and vomiting. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was normal, and empirical antibiotics were started for suspected meningitis. Abdominal examination revealed only mild diffuse tenderness without peritoneal signs. As symptoms persisted, a non-contrast computed tomography scan of the abdomen was performed on day six of hospitalization, revealing a 49 × 52 × 61 mm subcapsular liver abscess in segment VI with an air-fluid level, adjacent to a thickened appendix containing a 6 mm appendicolith, with localized fat plane obliteration. Laboratory investigations showed marked leukocytosis and elevated alkaline phosphatase, while transaminases remained normal. The patient underwent percutaneous abscess drainage and appendectomy. Abscess cultures grew Escherichia coli, and targeted antibiotic therapy was continued postoperatively. He was discharged with a liver drain, removed ten days after insertion. At one-week follow-up, complete clinical recovery was documented. Conclusions Pyogenic liver abscess secondary to acute appendicitis, though rare in the modern pediatric population, can still occur and may manifest with misleading extra-abdominal symptoms, such as altered consciousness mimicking central nervous system infection. This case underlines the importance of early abdominal imaging in the septic child without an obvious source. A coordinated multidisciplinary strategy combining source control, image-guided drainage, and pathogen-directed antibiotics leads to excellent outcomes.

title: Enterobius vermicularis and Appendicolith Co-occurrence in a Child with Prolonged Postprandial Abdominal Pain: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Enterobius vermicularis is occasionally identified in appendectomy specimens, but its clinical significance remains uncertain. The concurrent finding of E. vermicularis with an appendicolith in a child with atypical symptoms has rarely been reported in detail. Case presentation: An 8-year-old girl presented with a 10-day history of intermittent right lower quadrant pain consistently exacerbated after meals. She was afebrile, had localized tenderness without peritonitis, and all inflammatory markers were within normal limits. Non-contrast abdominal computed tomography revealed a calcified appendicolith obstructing a dilated appendix. During laparoscopic appendectomy, six live E. vermicularis organisms were recovered from the resected specimen. This intraoperative finding prompted meticulous stump management with double ligation, targeted suction, and peritoneal lavage to minimize the risk of parasite spillage. Histopathology showed acute inflammation superimposed on chronic changes with prominent lymphoid hyperplasia. Postoperative albendazole (400 mg orally, repeated after two weeks, with concurrent household treatment) achieved complete symptom resolution at three-month follow-up. title: Tensor Erasing-Based Data Augmentation for Fully Automated Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation
abstract: Abstract With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, deep learning has become a core technology for automated brain tumor segmentation via Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), providing critical morphological and positional information for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning—a typical medical computer vision application. However, scarce and imperfect high-quality annotated 3D MRI datasets severely restrict the training efficiency, generalization ability, and clinical utility of deep learning segmentation models. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel Tensor Erasing (TE) data augmentation method for 3D multi-modal brain tumor MRI segmentation, a generalizable strategy to enhance model robustness under data constraints. The core of TE is randomly selecting a specific-size 3D region from tensor-formatted MRI data, erasing voxel values by setting them to zero, and using these erased images as augmented training data. This simulates noisy or corrupted clinical images, forcing the model to focus on global tumor structures rather than local features, improving robustness and adaptability. Validated on the BraTS2019 dataset with 3D U-Net, Attention-UNet, and VGG-Net, TE consistently improves model performance. Specifically, the TE-augmented Attention-UNet achieves Dice coefficients of 87.15%, 82.77%, and 78.28% for whole tumor, tumor core, and enhancing tumor, respectively. As a low-cost, easy-to-implement strategy, TE alleviates data scarcity, enhances generalization, and can be extended to other computer vision tasks, laying a foundation for real-world deployment of intelligent vision systems.

title: Integrating NHANES and a Real-World Clinical Cohort to Evaluate the Consistent Dose-Response Association Between MHR and Osteoarthritis
abstract: Abstract Background Emerging evidence highlights the key role of chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic disorders in osteoarthritis (OA) pathogenesis. The monocyte-to-HDL-C ratio (MHR) serves as a promising integrated biomarker linking pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory status, yet its relationship with OA remains unclear. This study investigated the dose-response association between MHR and OA risk using the NHANES cohort and an independent clinical validation cohort with radiographic Kellgren-Lawrence grading. We further explored the potential mediating effect of body mass index (BMI) in this association. Methods This study adopted a two-stage discovery-validation design to investigate the association between MHR and OA. For the discovery phase, weighted data from 70,190 participants enrolled in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) during 2005–2018 were subjected to comprehensive statistical analysis. For the subsequent external validation phase, an independent clinical cohort comprising 500 hospital-based patients was utilized, with OA diagnosis in this cohort strictly established according to the K-L grading system. To assess the robustness of the association and its dose-response relationship, multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and subgroup analyses were applied across both study phases. Additionally, mediation analysis was conducted to quantify the proportion of the MHR-OA association mediated by body mass index (BMI). The clinical predictive value of MHR for OA was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), while two-piecewise linear regression analysis was employed to identify the optimal risk threshold of MHR for OA. Results In the NHANES cohort, MHR levels were significantly higher in patients with OA compared to non-OA participants ( P < 0.001). After full adjustment, MHR remained significantly associated with an increased risk of OA ( OR = 1.15, 95% CI : 1.04–1.26, P < 0.050). RCS regression revealed a consistent non-linear positive dose-response relationship, which was robust across most subgroups. Mediation analysis further indicated that BMI mediated 22.18% of the association between MHR and OA in the discovery cohort. These findings were successfully replicated in the independent clinical validation cohort, where BMI accounted for 23.01% of the total effect ( P < 0.001). Furthermore, MHR remained a strong independent predictor of OA ( OR = 2.64, 95% CI : 2.13–3.27, P < 0.001). In the clinical setting, MHR exhibited favorable diagnostic utility with an AUC of 0.839 (95% CI : 0.797–0.881, P < 0.001). Additionally, threshold effect analysis identified an inflection point at MHR = 4.12, beyond which the risk of OA increased significantly. Conclusion Our findings established MHR as a robust, independent, and cost-effective biomarker for OA risk, driven significantly by BMI-related metabolic pathways. The consistent results across population-based and clinical-based cohorts supported the use of MHR as a compelling tool for risk stratification and clinical screening.

title: A multi-agent system for spine MRI report generation from multi-sequence imaging
abstract: Abstract Spinal pathology is a leading cause of pain and disability worldwide. Spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to clinical evaluation, yet its interpretation remains complex and time-consuming, requiring integration of information across multiple imaging sequences and anatomical regions. Despite recent advances in automated MRI analysis, effectively combining multi-sequence data while preserving sequence-specific diagnostic information remains an open challenge. Here we present SpineAgent, a multi-agent framework for spine MRI report generation built upon a multi-sequence foundation model trained on routine clinical data from 32,047 patients and 453,683 MRI series, comprising a total of 13,441,191 MRI slices. To accommodate diverse modalities of sequences, we first pre-train two DINOv3-based encoders separately on T1- and T2-weighted sequences. We then introduce a continual training strategy that learns a synthesizer to embed images of other sequences using the T1 and T2 encoders, producing patient-level embedding that integrates various signals across MRI sequences. Using these embeddings, SpineAgent achieves state-of-the-art performance, with mean 10.8% AUROC improvement across 17 spinal condition-prediction tasks compared to the best competing method, and demonstrates strong generalizability under cross-manufacturer and cross-cohort evaluation. Beyond classification, SpineAgent enables pathology localization by identifying findings-relevant slices and segmenting pathological regions. It also supports multimodal image–report retrieval, providing a solid foundation for scalable and explainable MRI report generation. We further integrate these validated capabilities of SpineAgent into 37 specialized agents for condition diagnosis, pathological-region localization, and clinically-similar-cases retrieval. Finally, we incorporate their outputs as structured tokens within a Medical Report Agent trained end-to-end for report generation. Through both automated metrics and expert evaluation by five radiologists, SpineAgent achieves leading performance in spine MRI report generation. Together, SpineAgent introduces a continual training approach for multi-sequence spine MRI understanding. By decomposing report generation into clinically grounded subtasks addressed by specialized agents, the SpineAgent framework enables accurate, interpretable and generalizable spine MRI reporting across diverse imaging sequences and anatomical regions.

title: Adaptive edge-preserving denoising using a gradient-based delta-map for NDT X-ray imaging
abstract: Abstract In medical imaging and industrial non-destructive testing (NDT), preserving structural features while suppressing noise presents a fundamental trade-off. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes an adaptive image processing (AIP) technique utilizing a gradient-based delta-map (\(\:\delta\:\)-map) that generates pixel-wise weights based on the local gradient magnitudes. The proposed method quantifies the structural salience of the input image to generate a \(\:\delta\:\)-map and applies it to a residual-based enhancement process, thereby selectively suppressing noise in homogeneous regions while enhancing sharpness in edge regions. Experimental results on printed circuit board (PCB) X-ray images demonstrated that the proposed method yielded superior visual quality compared to conventional filters with globally fixed parameters (e.g., Gaussian, unsharp masking, bilateral) and commercial algorithms (MUSICA). Consistent performance improvements were confirmed through quantitative metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS) and no-reference image quality assessments (BRISQUE, NIQE). Furthermore, analysis of the modulation transfer function (MTF), noise power spectrum (NPS), and noise-equivalent quanta (NEQ) verified that the proposed method optimizes signal transfer characteristics across a wide frequency range while minimizing spatial resolution degradation. Unlike deep learning approaches, this method offers high computational efficiency and algorithmic interpretability, providing a practical solution immediately applicable to real-time X-ray inspection systems.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Using Normal Lung Radiomics and Dosiomics to Predict Radiation Pneumonitis After Lung Cancer Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to develop and interpret machine learning models based on radiomics and dosiomics features extracted from normal lung tissue after excluding the planning target volume for predicting grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis within 6 months after radiotherapy. Methods A total of 232 patients with lung cancer who received radiotherapy between February 2023 and June 2025 were retrospectively enrolled and divided into a training set (n = 162) and a validation set (n = 70). The region of interest was defined as the whole lung excluding the planning target volume. Radiomics features were extracted from pretreatment contrast-enhanced simulation CT images, and dosiomics features were extracted from three-dimensional RT Dose files using the same normal lung region. After preprocessing, LASSO regression and random forest were used for feature selection, and their intersecting features were retained. Eleven machine learning models were trained using five-fold cross-validation and evaluated in the validation set. Model performance was assessed using AUC, classification metrics, confusion matrix, and decision curve analysis. Kernel SHAP was applied for global model interpretation. Results Among all patients, 97 developed grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis, with an overall incidence of 41.8%. From 214 extracted features, 18 radiomics and dosiomics features were selected for modeling. Validation-set AUCs ranged from 0.725 to 0.812. LASSO and linear discriminant analysis achieved the highest AUCs, both 0.812; the 95% CI for LASSO was 0.708–0.917. The final LASSO model showed an accuracy of 74.3%, sensitivity of 58.1%, and specificity of 87.2%. SHAP analysis indicated that first-order, shape, and texture features jointly contributed to model prediction. Conclusion Radiomics and dosiomics features from normal lung tissue may provide complementary information for predicting grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis after lung cancer radiotherapy. The LASSO model showed favorable discrimination and interpretability in the validation set, but external validation is needed to further assess its stability and generalizability.

title: Brainana: an end-to-end preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging
abstract: Abstract Macaque MRI bridges non-invasive systems neuroscience with cellular and circuit-level mechanisms, but preprocessing remains fragmented across tools that are difficult to integrate, adapt to non-human primate acquisitions, and deploy reproducibly. We present Brainana, an automated, BIDS-compatible preprocessing framework for macaque neuroimaging. Brainana integrates structural and functional preprocessing, cortical surface reconstruction, quality control, transform tracking, and atlas projection within a containerized package, with cloud access for users without local compute. It incorporates macaque-trained deep learning models for brain extraction and tissue segmentation, conformation to standardize variable acquisitions, and surface reconstruction optimizations for macaque neuroanatomy. Across 23 imaging sites, Brainana processed data spanning heterogeneous scanners, protocols, species, and resolutions, yielding accurate anatomical correspondence across 130 monkeys, reliable native-space cortical surfaces, localized task-evoked activations, and reproducible brain-wide resting-state correlation structure. Brainana enables reproducible, scalable, and accessible macaque MRI preprocessing that supports cross-study comparison and multimodal integration across spatial scales, from neurons to networks.

title: Exploring Student and Faculty Insights on Ultrasound Education for Final-Year Medical Students: A Qualitative Study.
abstract: Background Ultrasound is an important bedside valuable tool, but its integration into undergraduate medical education remains variable, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. At Qatar University (QU) College of Medicine, ultrasound is introduced during the preclinical years, while clinical exposure remains largely opportunistic. This study explored student and faculty perspectives on the strengths and limitations of the ultrasound curriculum at QU. Methods A qualitative study used focus groups with final-year medical students (n=21) and semi-structured interviews with faculty involved in ultrasound training (n=15). Data were analyzed using a triangulated thematic approach combining independent manual coding with AI-assisted analysis. Final themes were refined through researcher consensus. Results The main finding was a translational gap between early technical proficiency and the ability to apply ultrasound findings to clinical reasoning and decision-making. Four student themes and five faculty themes emerged. Early preclinical exposure was valued for developing technical skills and confidence. However, clinical clerkship exposure was often opportunistic and lacked structured integration. Students reported confidence in image acquisition but limited exposure to pathology and clinical application. Faculty similarly recognized strong technical skills but identified weaknesses in interpretation, diagnostic reasoning, and clinical integration. Both groups supported a longitudinal, spiral curriculum with structured exposure to abnormal findings. Conclusion This study identifies a clear gap between technical ultrasound skills and their application in clinical practice. Bridging this gap requires moving from isolated preclinical teaching toward a longitudinal, clinically integrated curriculum that supports interpretation and clinical reasoning. These findings may inform ultrasound curriculum development in the MENA region and similar settings.

title: Coexistence of Erythrodermic Psoriasis and Bullous Pemphigoid: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Erythrodermic psoriasis (EP) represents a severe inflammatory subtype of psoriasis. Bullous pemphigoid (BP), the most common autoimmune subepidermal blistering disorder in clinical practice, predominantly affects elderly populations. Comorbidity of these two diseases is uncommon, and BP secondary to EP in young-adult patients is particularly rare. Case presentation A 33-year-old male with a 14-year relapsing-remitting history of psoriasis was admitted for erythrodermic psoriasis flare. Tense soybean-sized bullae with clear fluid appeared on bilateral lower extremities on the 5th hospital day. Skin biopsy demonstrated subepidermal blister formation with psoriasiform epidermal alterations. Direct immunofluorescence revealed basement-membrane-zone (BMZ) IgG (±) and C3 (+). Serum serology revealed markedly elevated levels of both anti-BP180 and anti-BP230 antibodies, whereas anti-desmoglein-1 and anti-desmoglein-3 antibodies were negative, supporting the diagnosis of coexisting EP and BP. The patient was treated with oral acitretin combined with high-potency topical halometasone cream, no new bullae occurred subsequently. Both psoriatic erythrodermic lesions and bullous lesions achieved marked improvement over the 6-month follow-up period. Conclusion This rare case of BP secondary to EP in a young adult underscores that clinicians should maintain high suspicion for BP when tense bullae develop de novo in patients with EP. Timely performance of histopathology, perilesional direct immunofluorescence, and pemphigoid-targeted serological testing is critical for establishing a definitive diagnosis.

title: Myxoid Onychomatricoma with Unusual CD99 Expression: A Report of a Rare Case and Literature Review.
abstract: Onychomatricoma (OM) is a rare, benign fibroepithelial tumor originating from the nail matrix, with different clinical and histological variants documented in existing studies. Myxoid OM is an even rarer subtype, characterized by a prominent fibromyxoid component in histopathology. We report a case of a 34-year-old male patient presenting with clinical manifestations consistent with typical OM. Histopathological examination revealed a biphasic tumor composed of an epithelial component and a prominent myxoid stroma, suggesting a diagnosis of myxoid OM. Notably, the tumor exhibited diffuse CD99 positivity, an extremely rare finding in OM. Histopathologically, myxoid OM shows considerable morphological overlap with superficial acral fibromyxoma (SAFM). Our case illustrates that CD99 positivity cannot serve as an absolute criterion to exclude OM; cautious interpretation of this marker is required to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in the differential diagnosis of these two entities. This case expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of myxoid OM and offers a valuable reference for its differential diagnosis. Furthermore, we include and provide a descriptive review to summarize the clinicopathological features and key differential diagnostic considerations of OM, with a focus on diagnostic pitfalls arising from rare histological variants and atypical immunophenotypes, to facilitate accurate differential diagnosis of subungual tumors.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Long-Term Follow-Up of Leukoencephalopathy in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia After Chemotherapy.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and long-term outcomes of leukoencephalopathy (LE) in pediatric patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) after chemotherapy, with the goal of evaluating diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis. Methods We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 48 pediatric ALL patients diagnosed with LE after chemotherapy at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University (February 2010-December 2024). Data included general information, Clinical manifestations and diagnostic imaging results. Compared with a control group of 27 healthy children, the patients' cognitive function was assessed by using the Behavioural Rating Inventory of Executive Function-2 (BRIEF-2) and the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Results Neurological symptoms were observed in 47.92% (23/48) of LE patients, including seizures (27.08%), paralysis (12.50%), limb numbness (10.42%), and speech impairment (10.42%). Brain MRI revealed white matter abnormalities, predominantly in the periventricular regions (47.92%), parietal lobes (37.50%), and frontal lobes (22.92%). Long-term follow-up demonstrated that 73.91% of symptomatic patients experienced rapid neurological improvement, and 83.33% of cases showed a significant reduction in MRI lesions within 12 months. Compared to controls, patients with LE exhibited higher BRIEF-2 scores (indicating executive dysfunction) for self-monitoring, emotional control, working memory, and planning/organization (all P < 0.05). The WISC scores were significantly lower for the total IQ, perceptual reasoning, working memory, and processing speed (P < 0.05). Conclusion Post-chemotherapy LE in pediatric ALL presents with diverse neurological symptoms and neuroimaging abnormalities accompanied by mild-to-moderate cognitive deficits. However, the prognosis appears favorable, with most patients showing symptom resolution and improved imaging findings.

title: Intramedullary Ependymoma of the Cervicomedullary Junction: Gross Total Resection and Surgical Nuances in an Anatomically Rare Location.
abstract: Background Intramedullary ependymomas are rare, slow-growing tumors (WHO grade II in most cases) arising from the ependymal cells of the spinal cord's central canal. In this case, histopathological examination confirmed a tanycytic ependymoma (WHO grade II). Although they have low potential for infiltration and seeding, and complete surgical excision is generally curative, the complex anatomy of the cervicomedullary region makes total resection particularly challenging. Case presentation We present the case of a 34-year-old woman who presented with subacute quadriparesis (McCormick grade III, MRC 3-4/5), diminished gag reflex, hyperreflexia, and spastic gait. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested the diagnosis of a cervicomedullary junction (CMJ) ependymoma and definitive diagnosis was established histopathologically. The patient underwent successful microscopic total resection via a posterior midline approach, including suboccipital craniectomy, C1 and C2 laminectomy, and midline myelotomy, all performed under intraoperative neuromonitoring. At one-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated improvement to McCormick grade I with MRC grade 5/5 in all limbs. Postoperative MRI confirmed complete resection without evidence of local recurrence. Conclusion Neurological recovery was assessed using the McCormick Scale and Medical Research Council (MRC) muscle strength grading. The patient improved from a preoperative McCormick grade III (significant motor weakness requiring assistance for ambulation) to grade I (normal neurological function) at one-year follow-up. MRC muscle strength improved from 3-4/5 in all limbs preoperatively to 5/5 in all limbs postoperatively. Postoperative MRI at one-year follow-up confirmed complete resection without evidence of local recurrence. This case suggests that gross total resection of cervicomedullary ependymomas under intraoperative neuromonitoring is achievable and can result in excellent neurological outcomes, highlighting the importance of precise microsurgical techniques and intraoperative monitoring in managing these challenging tumors.

title: Thyroid Cancer in the Modern Era: From Molecular Landscape and Multimodal Diagnostics to Integrative Traditional Chinese Medicine-A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: In recent decades, the global incidence of thyroid cancer has risen sharply mainly due to the high detection rate of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma and overdiagnosis, with its overall mortality staying steady. Classic pathogenic drivers encompass childhood radiation exposure, iodine disorder, and hallmark gene alterations including BRAF V600E, RET/PTC, RAS and PAX8/PPARγ. Modern multimodal diagnostic systems integrating artificial intelligence-assisted high-resolution ultrasound, Thyroseq-V2, Afirma, circulating tumor DNA detection and refined pathological examination achieve precise preoperative stratification. Aberrant activation of MAPK/ERK, PI3K/AKT and Wnt/β-catenin cascades, coupled with an immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by M2-type tumor-associated macrophages, regulatory T cells and PD-L1 overexpression, drives thyroid cancer progression and dedifferentiation. Current comprehensive integrated therapeutic strategies cover robotic surgery, radioactive iodine ablation, external radiotherapy, molecular targeted drugs (sorafenib, lenvatinib, vemurafenib combined with trametinib) and novel immunotherapy. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), based on the TCM pathogenesis of liver qi stagnation, phlegm-blood stasis and qi-blood deficiency for goiter, serves as an adjuvant therapy for thyroid cancer. Active ingredients such as honokiol, artesunate, ginsenoside Rg3, astragalus polysaccharide and curcumin can suppress tumor proliferation, reshape anti-tumor immunity and inhibit metastasis via regulating reactive oxygen species, PI3K/AKT pathway, epithelial-mesenchymal transition and matrix metalloproteinases. Existing clinical observations confirm that TCM can relieve clinical discomfort, improve life quality and lower recurrence risk when combined with conventional radioiodine or anti-tumor treatment. However, the clinical application of TCM for thyroid cancer is greatly restricted by insufficient syndrome differentiation standardization, low-quality clinical evidence and unclear herbal safety risks. Most available studies are small-sample retrospective analyses lacking large-scale, multicenter randomized controlled trials to verify efficacy and safety. Future research should focus on standardized clinical trial design, in-depth pharmacological mechanism exploration, and construction of standardized thyroid cancer integrative diagnosis and treatment regimens combining Western precision therapy and TCM adjuvant intervention, to clarify the definite positioning of TCM in whole-course thyroid cancer management.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Infraspinatus-Teres Minor Interfascial Block versus Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block for Analgesia After Arthroscopic Shoulder Surgery: A Randomized Non-Inferiority Clinical Trial.
abstract: Background This randomized non-inferiority trial was designed to verify whether ultrasound-guided infraspinatus-teres minor interfascial block (ITMB) could produce non-inferior postoperative analgesia in adult patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder surgery compared with ultrasound-guided interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB), while also comparing the early respiratory safety profiles and postoperative adverse events of the two techniques. Methods This trial adopted a two-arm parallel-group design with blinding for participants and all outcome assessors. A total of 82 eligible patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive either ITMB (n=41) or ISB (n=41) with 25 mL 0.375% ropivacaine for each nerve block. Two participants in the ITMB group were excluded from the per-protocol (PP) analysis due to intraoperative conversion to open surgery and unplanned intensive care unit admission, leaving 39 ITMB patients and 41 ISB patients for primary PP analysis; intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis covering all 82 randomized patients was additionally conducted to validate robustness. The primary prespecified outcome was 24-hour postoperative total oxycodone consumption, with a predefined non-inferiority margin of -5 mg (ISB minus ITMB). Non-inferiority was established if the lower limit of the 95% confidence interval (CI) for the between-group mean difference was no less than -5 mg. Secondary endpoints comprised the maximum 11-point resting NRS pain score within 24 h, incidence of rebound pain, and rescue analgesia requirements. Safety endpoints included dyspnea, diaphragmatic paralysis, Horner's syndrome, and postoperative nausea and vomiting. Results PP analysis showed the mean 24-hour oxycodone consumption was 11.26 (SD 4.38) mg in the ISB group (95% CI 9.89 to 12.65) versus 10.92 (SD 3.48) mg in the ITMB group (95% CI 9.79 to 12.05), with a between-group mean difference of 0.34 mg (95% CI -1.42 to 2.11, P <0.001). The lower bound of the 95% CI (-1.42 mg) substantially exceeded the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -5 mg, satisfying the non-inferiority criterion (one-sided non-inferiority P <0.001). ITT analysis yielded consistent non-inferiority results (mean difference 0.26 mg, 95% CI -1.46 to 1.99, P <0.001). For secondary pain outcomes, the median worst resting NRS score within 24 h was significantly lower in the ITMB group [3.0 (IQR 3.0-4.0)] than the ISB group [4.0 (IQR 3.0-7.0), median difference 1.0, 95% CI 0 to 1.0, P <0.001]. ITMB also brought significantly lower rebound pain rate (2.6% vs 26.8%, P =0.006) and less frequent rescue analgesia requirements (7.7% vs 29.3%, P =0.016). Safety outcomes revealed significantly lower early hemidiaphragmatic paralysis and dyspnea in the ITMB group: hemidiaphragmatic paralysis occurred in only 2.6% of ITMB patients vs 90.2% of ISB patients ( P <0.001); dyspnea incidence was 2.6% (ITMB) vs 19.5% (ISB, P =0.016); Horner's syndrome was absent in the ITMB group while occurring in 29% of ISB patients ( P <0.001). Postoperative nausea and vomiting rates were comparable between two groups ( P =0.655). No severe block-related complications such as nerve injury, local anesthetic systemic toxicity or pneumothorax were observed in either group. Conclusion Ultrasound-guided ITMB provided non-inferior 24-hour postoperative opioid analgesia compared with ISB and reduced the incidence of early hemidiaphragmatic paralysis in patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder surgery. The comparable total 24-hour oxycodone consumption reflected distinct time-dependent analgesic profiles, with ISB providing greater analgesic benefit during the early postoperative period, whereas ITMB demonstrated more sustained analgesic effects during the later postoperative period. Trial registration This trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400084716). Date of registration: May 23, 2024.

title: Advances in Drug Delivery Systems for Breast Cancer: From Microenvironment Barriers and Smart Carriers to Clinical Translation Strategies.
abstract: Breast cancer heterogeneity and its complex tumor microenvironment (TME) are key drivers of therapeutic failure and multidrug resistance (MDR). Drug delivery systems (DDS) provide an important approach, but their clinical translation remains limited by biological variability, formulation complexity, and manufacturing challenges. This review delineates the evolution of breast cancer DDS from passive carriers to increasingly functional and responsive platforms, focusing on three core dimensions. First, regarding decisive barriers, we dissect the constraints imposed by the three-dimensional collagen network, pH/glutathione (GSH) gradients, and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) on drug penetration. These factors not only act as physical and biochemical obstacles but can also be harnessed as endogenous triggers for responsive design. Second, in terms of diversified platforms, we critically evaluate liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, hydrogels, extracellular vesicles, and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We highlight the potential of solid lipid nanoparticles to address drug resistance, the development of carrier-free delivery enabled by prodrug self-assembly, and the clinical significance of ADCs (eg, T-DXd) in expanding treatment options for HER2-low breast cancer. Third, we examine inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, metastatic site-specific delivery barriers in the brain, bone, and lung, the multilayered resistance network from efflux pumps to cancer stem cells, and the sequential barriers nanomedicines must traverse from systemic circulation to intracellular targets. We propose three strategic directions: personalized precision delivery integrating liquid biopsy, organoids, and functional imaging to support patient stratification and treatment adaptation; AI-assisted formulation optimization using machine learning to develop material-structure-function predictive models and support data-driven formulation design; and multi-responsive systems leveraging endogenous signals such as pH, GSH, and enzymes, together with exogenous stimuli including light, magnetism, and ultrasound, for spatiotemporally controlled combination therapy. This review summarizes key considerations from biological barriers to clinical translation, emphasizing that alignment of tumor subtype, metastatic site, microenvironmental characteristics, and patient-specific factors may improve the clinical applicability of drug delivery strategies.
